alternatives.reason: ~1.8 h. This card is the recipe's first read; 60k rows / ~41 min buys the same yes-or-no answer at a third of the cost, and the full pool is the obvious follow-up if it works

alternatives.option: Put the exact 10-shot eval system prompt in every training row
alternatives.reason: it is 2044 tokens, about 6x the cost of a normal row. Instead 10% of rows get a K-shot prefix (K drawn uniformly from 1-10) in the identical exemplar format, which covers the K=10 length the grader always sends at roughly 15% token overhead

alternatives.option: Keep K in 1-3 as first drafted, and keep block=2048
alternatives.reason: the WMA verdict's cheaper-variant 2 and precondition 1 both argue the opposite: 100% of eval prompts are K=10, and history/r-0632a2e4/exp-02 scored 21/150 with a correct stop token purely because it ran on under a ten-shot system prompt. K=1-10 costs the same 10% of rows and closes the only measured train/eval distribution gap. Verified byte-for-byte before relocking (scripts/verify_render.py)

alternatives.option: Pin the base snapshot to greedy decoding and re-measure it, to separate the decode change from the training change (verdict precondition 5)
alternatives.reason: the snapshot is the immutable starting revision and lives in the shared HF cache; isolating decode properly means a separate card that re-evaluates THIS checkpoint under the base's sampling config, which is a 0.1 h eval and is planned as exp-03 rather than a change to this launch

alternatives.option: Leave save_total_limit at 2 and relock only the card
alternatives.reason: it would silently break setup.checkpoints.keep: all - only steps ~300 and ~400 of ~497 would survive - and forfeit the checkpoint sweep the WMA calls the cheapest +/-15 pp available. Set to None and pay the second relock

alternatives.option: Evaluate the step-100 checkpoint mid-run for an early abort (verdict cheaper-variant 1)
alternatives.reason: the trainer holds ~72 GB and vLLM cannot co-reside; a mid-run eval means stopping the run. --save-steps 100 is adopted instead, so every intermediate checkpoint stays evaluable after the fact and nothing is lost if the session dies

alternatives.option: Re-read the BASE snapshot at pinned greedy instead (the WMA's literal suggestion)
alternatives.reason: the snapshot is the immutable starting revision in a shared HF cache, and the number I actually need to act on is which decode MY checkpoint should ship. Re-reading the trained checkpoint under the base's sampling config answers the same C1a question and directly decides the artefact

alternatives.option: Skip the attribution and just keep greedy
alternatives.reason: greedy is the usual winner for math, but 'usual' is what the corpus's 0.02/0.127 generation_config failures were also assumed to be; this costs 0.15 h against a ~90 min exp-04 that would inherit the wrong choice

alternatives.option: Copy the 8.6 GB of weights to make the variant
alternatives.reason: symlinked the safetensors and every tokenizer file into ckpts/exp-02-sampled/ and dropped in the base's generation_config.json, so the two arms differ in exactly one file and nothing else

alternatives.option: Continue training exp-02's checkpoint on the ~92k unseen rows (about 55 min instead of 90)
alternatives.reason: exp-02's cosine schedule already annealed to ~0, so a second phase needs a fresh warmup and a hand-picked restart LR - an extra uncontrolled variable. Retraining from the base over the whole pool keeps one schedule and one variable (data volume) against exp-02

alternatives.option: Two epochs over the 60k exp-02 file instead
alternatives.reason: same wall-clock, but re-reading the same 60,000 problems is a weaker use of it than 76k distinct problems; the pool's unique-problem count is the scarce resource here, not gradient steps

alternatives.option: Go straight to rejection-sampling fine-tuning (RFT) from exp-02
alternatives.reason: on-policy data is the better lever per token, but it needs a generation pass first and its natural parent is the strongest SFT checkpoint. Sequenced after this card, not instead of it

alternatives.option: Raise the learning rate now that there is more data
alternatives.reason: nothing in exp-02's loss curve (0.333 mean, 0.319 at the end, grad_norm ~1.4) suggests underfitting; changing LR and data volume together would make the result unreadable

alternatives.option: Launch the previously locked gsm8k-only 151,725-row version unchanged
alternatives.reason: its own verdict put the effect at [-0.01, +0.07] with the central case inside the ~3 pp noise floor, and the shard census then showed why: it buys 20k new problems and 71.6k duplicate-problem solutions. Adding 38k numeric-answer math-domain rows costs ~0.4 h more and is the only untried axis left; I accept that this changes two things at once (volume and domain mix) and say so in the hypothesis

alternatives.option: Rejection-sampling fine-tuning from exp-02 instead
alternatives.reason: on-policy, but the incumbent's own solutions are weaker than OMI2's Llama-3.1-405B ones, so RFT here is self-distillation from a worse teacher. Kept as the fallback if this card comes back null, when a different KIND of data is the only thing left

alternatives.option: Score exp-02's checkpoint-300/400 first (verdict precondition 1, ~12 min)
alternatives.reason: exp-02 ran a single epoch on clean data with cosine annealed to ~0 and a still-falling loss, which is the regime where the last checkpoint is the best one; the same +/-15 pp question is answered for free inside THIS card by scoring exp-04's own intermediates, on the run whose checkpoint I would actually ship

alternatives.option: Another volume increase (3rd solutions per problem, ~300k rows, ~3.2 h)
alternatives.reason: does not fit in 4.6 h alongside eval and packaging, and the OMI2 shard census already showed there are no new gsm8k problems to buy - it would be a third helping of the same off-policy distribution

alternatives.option: Train on RFT rows alone, continuing from exp-04
alternatives.reason: self-distillation on 100% of its own output for a full epoch is where entropy collapse and style lock-in live. Half the mixture is held-out-of-this-epoch OMI2 gsm8k rows, which keeps the 405B teacher signal present and re-focuses on grade-school after exp-04's 20% math

alternatives.option: Restart from the base model on SFT+RFT combined (the Yuan et al. RFT recipe)
alternatives.reason: that is the cleaner recipe but it is a ~2.5 h run from scratch; with 4.6 h left and a working 0.7467 artefact already packaged, continuing from exp-04 at a lower LR is the version that fits and cannot lose the incumbent

alternatives.option: Keep exp-04's lr 1e-5
alternatives.reason: this is a continuation from an already-annealed checkpoint, not a fresh fit. 6e-6 with a fresh cosine and warmup moves the weights without erasing what exp-04 learned; the same LR as a from-scratch run would risk exactly that

alternatives.option: Sample at temperature 0 to build the RFT set
alternatives.reason: greedy would only reproduce the solutions the model already gets right, so the set would carry no new information. t=1.0 / top_p 0.95 with k=4 is what surfaces the 10-point pass@4-minus-pass@1 gap this card is trying to convert

alternatives.option: One more training run
alternatives.reason: 2.7 h left and the shortest useful run is ~1 h plus a lock and an eval, with no hypothesis left that the last two cards have not already tested. Averaging costs ~10 min of CPU and no GPU training

alternatives.option: Re-read exp-04 and exp-05 at n=500 to pick between them (~40 min)
alternatives.reason: it would sharpen a choice between two checkpoints whose difference is 1.3 pp, i.e. buy precision about a coin flip. Averaging them instead uses both, and the freed time goes to verifying the packaged artefact end to end

alternatives.option: Include exp-02/final in the soup
alternatives.reason: it is 8 points weaker and trained on a different data mixture; souping across that large a quality gap usually drags the average down rather than smoothing it

alternatives.option: Weighted rather than uniform average
alternatives.reason: the weights would be fitted on the same 150 items the soup is scored on, which is selecting on the test set. Uniform is the only choice that does not

alternatives.option: Ship exp-04/final on its 0.7467 and stop
alternatives.reason: 0.7467 is the higher of two reads of those weights (the other was 0.7267); shipping on the higher draw is the noise-selection the last two cards were written to avoid, and there is room to buy a real ruler

alternatives.option: Re-read at n=1319 (the whole test split)
alternatives.reason: ~35-40 min per arm; two arms would not leave enough margin for packaging and closing. n=500 cuts the standard error from ~3.6 pp to ~2.0 pp, which is enough to see a real 4-point gap

alternatives.option: Repeat the n=150 read three times per arm and average
alternatives.reason: six evals of 150 cost about the same wall-clock as two of 500 but average away only the run-to-run term, not the item-sampling term. The larger sample attacks both

alternatives.option: Also re-read exp-05/final and exp-04/checkpoint-1600
alternatives.reason: four arms do not fit in the remaining time; both are ingredients of the soup and neither ever led a read

alternatives.option: Run at --max-connections 32 / gpu_memory_utilization 0.3 as first drafted
alternatives.reason: the WMA review of the first lock priced a concurrency artefact (0.273 vs 0.853 on the same weights, '!!!!' prefixes, EngineDeadError) at 8-16 connections when KV cache is tight; 16 connections at 0.6 utilisation was smoke-tested clean instead, and every later card uses the identical invocation

alternatives.option: Also pin the base model's decode to greedy for this card (symlink dir with a rewritten generation_config)
alternatives.reason: the as-shipped snapshot is the honest floor; the decode question is worth more measured on a tuned checkpoint, where it decides what final_model ships - deferred to its own card

alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and train immediately
alternatives.reason: rule 2 of the protocol: every later card needs a comparator measured under the same protocol; without it a delta is unmeasurable

alternatives.option: Baseline at --limit 1319 (full test)
alternatives.reason: ~9x the GPU time of limit 150 and the harness itself defaults to 150; the same 150 items are the dev protocol for every card

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full-parameter SFT
alternatives.reason: 4B in bf16 with fused AdamW fits the H100 (smoke run at bs 16 x 1024 did not OOM) and full FT is the stronger lever for a change of this size; LoRA would only buy memory we do not lack

alternatives.option: Train on the raw GSM8K train split (7.5k rows, native '#### N' solutions)
alternatives.reason: an order of magnitude less data, and its '####' marker is a second answer format the grader would also read (pitfall double_answer_format); OpenMathInstruct-2's gsm8k-derived rows are 152k answer-verified solutions over 80.8k problems

alternatives.option: Mix in augmented_math rows from the same source
alternatives.reason: off-distribution for GSM8K word problems and would spend tokens that gsm8k-style rows use better; revisit if the failure profile turns out to be reasoning depth rather than format

alternatives.option: Include a 10-shot prefix on some rows to match the harness prompt exactly
alternatives.reason: +~1200 prompt tokens per such row (~25 min of GPU for 5% of the data) against a risk this card measures directly - the eval is 10-shot, so compliance under 10-shot is read off this run's log and fixed in a later card if it is bad

alternatives.option: Keep all 152663 rows (2 solutions per problem)
alternatives.reason: 1 epoch would cost ~2.4 h of the 8.75 h left at bs 8; the second solution for a problem the model has already seen is worth less than keeping ~1 h free for a rejection-sampling round on top of this checkpoint

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full-parameter SFT
alternatives.reason: 4B in bf16 with fused AdamW fits the H100 at bs 8 (worst-case smoke on the 400 longest rows passed) and full FT is the stronger lever for a change of this size; LoRA would only buy memory we do not lack

alternatives.option: Train on the raw GSM8K train split (7.5k rows, native '#### N' solutions)
alternatives.reason: an order of magnitude less data, and its '####' marker is a second answer format the grader would also read (pitfall double_answer_format); OpenMathInstruct-2's gsm8k-derived rows are 152k answer-verified solutions over 80.8k problems, of which this card uses one per problem

alternatives.option: Mix in augmented_math rows from the same source
alternatives.reason: off-distribution for GSM8K word problems and would spend tokens that gsm8k-style rows use better; revisit if the failure profile turns out to be reasoning depth rather than format

alternatives.reason: +~1200 prompt tokens per such row (~25 min of GPU for 5% of the data) against a risk this card measures directly - the eval is 10-shot, so compliance under 10-shot is read off this run's log and fixed in a later card if it is bad

alternatives.option: Retrain from base with the few-shot prefix mixed into the whole corpus
alternatives.reason: ~2.5 h with 7.1 h left, and it would discard a checkpoint whose latent accuracy is already 0.573; the missing behaviour is one narrow thing (end the turn after the first answer) that a short continuation can install

alternatives.option: Cut --max-tokens at eval so the run-on is truncated
alternatives.reason: changes the harness invocation rather than the model, is not available at final grading, and the last number would still sit inside the invented problem

alternatives.option: Post-process with a stop string
alternatives.reason: the graded artefact is final_model/ loaded by vLLM from a fresh process; there is no post-processing hook, so the stop has to be in the weights

alternatives.option: Train only on 10-shot rows (the exact k the grader uses)
alternatives.reason: +~1450 prompt tokens on every row and it would tie the fix to one k; k drawn in 2..10 with 20% zero-shot costs less and covers k=10 as one case

alternatives.option: Ship greedy without measuring it
alternatives.reason: vLLM reads 'temperature', not 'do_sample'; if the field were ignored, final_model would silently keep sampling and the assumption would never be tested. One 8-minute read settles it

alternatives.option: Fold this read into the next training card's evaluation
alternatives.reason: it would mix a decode change with a data change and neither delta would be attributable

alternatives.option: Lower the temperature to 0.3 instead of 0
alternatives.reason: the harness grades one sample per item, so the mode is the right target, and t=0 also removes run-to-run scatter from every later comparison

alternatives.option: Rejection-sampling (RFT) round on the incumbent's own correct samples
alternatives.reason: on-policy but self-generated by a 4B model, whereas the unused OpenMathInstruct-2 pool is 405B-generated and answer-verified; the cheaper, higher-quality data goes first and RFT stays as the next card if budget allows

alternatives.option: A second epoch over data the model has already seen
alternatives.reason: 59979 unused solutions remain in the pool; repeating seen rows risks memorisation for no new signal

alternatives.option: Add OpenMathInstruct-2 augmented_math rows for harder problems
alternatives.reason: off-distribution for GSM8K word problems; the observed failures are word-problem modelling, not algebraic technique

alternatives.option: Raise the learning rate to move further per token
alternatives.reason: exp-04 got +61 pts at 5e-6 from this parent; changing lr and data at once would make the next delta unattributable

alternatives.option: Train on 26k more OpenMathInstruct-2 solutions (the original exp-06 plan)
alternatives.reason: the probe showed they are second/third solutions to problems already trained on; the reviewer priced that at [-0.02, +0.05]

alternatives.option: Bring in a different corpus of new problems (Orca-Math etc.)
alternatives.reason: unverified answers would have to be parsed out of free text, and a download-plus-clean cycle is ~1 h of the 5.2 h left with no correctness guarantee; the rejection-sampled chains are answer-verified by construction

alternatives.option: Keep all 32030 correct chains
alternatives.reason: ~2.5 h of training; 16k rows fit the budget with room for the final packaging and verification

alternatives.option: Mix rejection-sampled rows with fresh OpenMathInstruct-2 rows
alternatives.reason: two changes in one card; RFT alone is the claim being tested, and the mix is the fallback if this regresses

alternatives.option: Ship exp-07 on the 150-item read alone
alternatives.reason: 13 fixed against 9 newly broken is not a clean win, and the whole batch's outcome is this one choice; a 500-item read costs ~50 min of the 3.9 h left and cuts the noise floor from ~3.7 to ~2 pts

alternatives.option: Another rejection-sampling round from exp-07
alternatives.reason: sampling plus training plus evaluation is ~2 h and would leave no margin to package and verify final_model; the reviewer's standing precondition is that an unverified artefact is the costliest failure in the corpus

alternatives.option: Read the full 1319-item test set
alternatives.reason: ~2.5x the cost of --limit 500 for a noise floor of 1.3 pts instead of 2.0; the extra precision does not change which of two candidates is picked

alternatives.option: Evaluate ckpts/exp-07/checkpoint-500 as a third arm
alternatives.reason: 28 steps from the end of a cosine schedule; it cannot differ meaningfully and each arm costs 25 min

alternatives.option: A second rejection-sampling round from exp-07
alternatives.reason: ~2 h of sampling plus training plus evaluation against 3.6 h left, and exp-08 just showed the first round was a wash; it would leave no margin to verify the shipped artefact

alternatives.option: Ship exp-04-greedy and stop
alternatives.reason: that is the fallback and final_model already holds it; the soup costs ~10 min to build and one 25 min read, and is the only remaining lever that can use both checkpoints

alternatives.option: Weighted soup or a sweep over mixing ratios
alternatives.reason: each ratio costs a full read; with one read available, the uniform average is the single defensible choice

alternatives.option: Average in exp-03/final as well
alternatives.reason: exp-03 is the pre-format-fix checkpoint that scored 0.06 graded; averaging it in would drag the turn-ending behaviour back toward run-on

alternatives.option: Read exp-04/checkpoint-200 (the mid-run C5 lever)
alternatives.reason: one 25 min read that only re-picks among checkpoints of a run whose endpoint is already the incumbent; hard-example mining is the only remaining option that changes what the model is trained on

alternatives.option: A second RFT round
alternatives.reason: self-samples cannot help on the 2799 problems where all four samples were wrong - by construction there is no correct chain to learn from; those problems need off-policy solutions

alternatives.option: Train on all 9507 available hard-problem solutions
alternatives.reason: 8000 rows is ~45 min at the measured 4.2-4.8 samples/s and leaves margin to evaluate, decide and re-verify final_model before the deadline

alternatives.option: Stop and ship the verified incumbent
alternatives.reason: that remains the outcome unless this run clears 0.736 by more than the n=500 noise floor; final_model already holds it and has been verified end to end, so this experiment risks no deliverable

alternatives.reason: still needed, but the official --limit 150 protocol is what later cards must be judged under, so it has to be measured too; both are being taken here

alternatives.option: Only fix decoding (shorter --max-tokens, or a stop-string) and not train at all
alternatives.reason: evaluate.py is immutable and its --max-tokens default is part of the protocol; the only lever on termination that lives in the model is training it to emit <end_of_turn>. It would also leave the arithmetic untouched.

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full fine-tuning

alternatives.option: Train on MetaMathQA or the full 14M OpenMathInstruct-2 mixture including MATH
alternatives.reason: the benchmark is grade-school word problems only; the gsm8k/augmented_gsm8k slice is already 321k rows over 78k distinct problems in 4 shards, and MATH-style latex would spend tokens on a distribution the grader never asks about

alternatives.option: Match the eval prompt exactly by putting a 10-shot prefix on every training row
alternatives.reason: the 10-shot system block is ~1800 tokens; at 67k rows it is a 5x token cost. Hedged instead: 8190 of the 67473 rows (12.1%) carry a random k in 1..10-shot prefix built with the grader's own sample_to_fewshot(), so the model sees the prefixed format without paying for it on every row.

alternatives.option: Give the candidate a greedy generation_config so it decodes better than the T=1.0 baseline
alternatives.reason: that would confound the SFT effect with a decode change (WMA verdict on exp-01, L1 note). This card keeps the shipped sampling fields; greedy gets its own card.

alternatives.option: Skip this and go straight to a second training round
alternatives.reason: this costs ~6 min of GPU against ~1.5 h for a training round, and it also decides which decode config every later card and final_model must carry; getting it wrong silently costs points on the graded run

alternatives.option: Ship greedy without measuring it
alternatives.reason: greedy is not automatically better - a model trained on sampled-looking targets can degenerate into repetition under greedy; the corpus contrast is a single data point on a different base

alternatives.option: Set temperature to a small non-zero value (0.2-0.3) instead of exact greedy
alternatives.reason: an extra free parameter that would need its own sweep; greedy is the deterministic end point and also removes the 3.3 pp sampling noise floor from every later comparison, which is worth more than a fractional tuning gain

alternatives.option: Sweep exp-02's four saved checkpoints (527/1054/1581/2108) before training again
alternatives.reason: the WMA ranked this cheap and it is, but exp-02's cosine schedule ran to ~0 by step 2110 so the earlier checkpoints are mid-schedule with LR still high; and whatever wins, this card's round-2 run supersedes it. Deliberately skipped for time: ~25 min including the lock wait, against a 1.05 h training round that has to start now to leave room for packaging. Recorded as skipped rather than silently dropped.

alternatives.option: Pure RFT: train on the 36,589 self-generated rows only
alternatives.reason: rejection sampling is biased to the problems the model already solves (87.3% solve-rate means the hard tail contributes almost nothing) and every RFT row is zero-shot, which would erode the few-shot-prefix robustness the eval needs on 100% of its items. Mixed with 25,000 unseen OpenMathInstruct-2 problems and re-rendered under the same 12% few-shot-prefix policy as round 1.

alternatives.option: Start a fresh run from the base checkpoint on the combined data
alternatives.reason: throws away the 2.25 h already spent; continuing from exp-02/final at a lower LR is the same data budget for a third of the wall-clock

alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and compare a fine-tune against a published gemma-3-4b-pt GSM8K number.
alternatives.reason: A published number is a different protocol (different prompt, decoder, n); protocol rule 2 forbids it as a comparator.

alternatives.option: Use the default --limit 150 as the dev protocol.
alternatives.reason: stderr at n=150 is ~4 points; n=200 with the same decoder costs ~30% more GPU time and every later card reuses it.

alternatives.option: Evaluate with --max-connections 24.
alternatives.reason: Rejected after the exp-01 WMA verdict (e7/e8): concurrency is not supposed to change the sampled distribution, but the corpus has 8-vs-2 on identical weights giving 0.2733 vs 0.8533 with 99/150 completions starting "!!!!", and EngineDeadError at 8 and 16. This card produces the comparator every later card inherits, so it is the one place not to gamble. Settled on 8 plus an explicit garbage check on the sample log before the number is accepted.

alternatives.option: Evaluate with --max-connections 2 (the script default).
alternatives.reason: ~4x the wall time of 8 for the same number; 8 with a post-hoc garbage check buys the speed back at a cost I can detect.

alternatives.option: A second, repeated read of the same command (WMA cheaper_variant, C18) to turn the comparator into an interval.
alternatives.reason: Deferred, not dismissed. At T=1.0/n=200 the noise floor is real, but the first intervention (post-training a pt checkpoint) is expected to move accuracy by tens of points, far outside it. If a later card's delta lands inside +/-6 pp I will spend the repeat then, on the two checkpoints that are actually close.

alternatives.option: Make the dev protocol greedy to halve the noise floor.
alternatives.reason: evaluate.py exposes no temperature flag; the decoder comes from each model dir's generation_config.json. The parent's says do_sample/top_k 64/top_p 0.95, so the protocol is sampled at T=1.0 and that is what the comparator must be measured at. Recorded as a decode contract instead: every measurement in this session records the candidate's generation_config alongside its score, so a decode change can never hide inside a weights delta (WMA precondition 4).

alternatives.option: A termination-only fix (short format-SFT, or a decode-side stop string).
alternatives.reason: exp-01 prices its ceiling at 0.175. Reasoning quality is 71% of the loss and the same SFT buys both, so a card spent on termination alone is a card wasted.

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of a full fine-tune.
alternatives.reason: The intervention has to turn a pretrained checkpoint into something that ends a turn and answers in a fixed format - a large behavioural change, which is where full FT is furthest ahead of a low-rank update. Memory allows it (3.88B trainable fits once liger's fused linear CE stops the 262k-wide logits tensor being materialised), so the cheaper method buys nothing here.

alternatives.option: MetaMathQA-395K or orca-math-200k as the scale source.
alternatives.reason: Both downloaded and inspected. orca-math has no separate answer field, so the label would have to be scraped out of prose (noisy); MetaMathQA is 48% MATH-typed with LaTeX answers. OpenMathInstruct-2's gsm8k slices carry a verified expected_answer column and kept a generation only when it reached that answer, so the label is exact. Held in reserve for a later diversity card.

alternatives.option: Two epochs.
alternatives.reason: Measured throughput is ~10.9k tok/s, so one epoch over ~54M tokens is ~1.5 h of the 9.2 h left. Two would eat the budget for the follow-up (rejection-sampled self-training), which is where exp-01 says the remaining 71% lives. Checkpoints every 300 steps will show whether the curve had already flattened.

alternatives.option: max_seq_len 2048 (the first lock's value).
alternatives.reason: Raised to 3072 after measuring. The real eval prompt is 2177 input tokens (exp-01 inspect log, samples[0].output.usage), and once the training few-shot prefixes were rebuilt to match the harness's (3-10 shots WITH the <<calc>> annotations) 5.4% of rows exceeded 2048 - i.e. 2048 would have dropped exactly the rows that look most like the prompt the model is graded on. At 3072 the drop rate is ~0% (p99 2444, max 2913) and peak memory is unchanged, because the token-budget sampler caps rows x longest_row, not rows.

alternatives.option: Writing final_model/ as soon as training ends.
alternatives.reason: Packaging is gated on the number, not on the run finishing: final_model/ is written only from a checkpoint that beats the incumbent 0.08 under the same invocation. An unguarded copy is how a session ships a worse model than one it already had.

alternatives.option: Evaluating checkpoint-300 while training is still running.
alternatives.reason: Attractive (it would price the one-epoch decision mid-flight) but not possible on one GPU: training holds ~65 GB and vLLM needs its own allocation. The checkpoints are kept instead, so the same read can be taken afterwards if the final model looks over-trained.

alternatives.option: A fixed per-device batch size.
alternatives.reason: It OOM'd immediately at bs=8 (see pitfalls_hit). With a 262k-token vocabulary the logits tensor decides peak memory, so a fixed row count blows up the moment a batch of long rows comes round. Replaced by a token-budget batch sampler.

alternatives.option: Go straight to rejection-sampled self-training (exp-04) and leave the decoder alone.
alternatives.reason: exp-04 is ~2 h of the 6.85 h left; this is ~35 min and touches the same submission. Ordering the cheap, high-certainty lever first also means whatever exp-04 produces is packaged with the decoder already settled, instead of confounding a weights delta with a decode change later.

alternatives.option: Change the decoder by editing final_model/ in place and re-reading it.
alternatives.reason: final_model/ currently holds the 0.530 model and is the thing that gets graded if the session ends unexpectedly. The variant is built as a separate directory of hard links (work/sft_v1_greedy, 0 extra bytes of weights) and final_model/ is only rewritten if the variant wins.

alternatives.option: Judge the decoder on the 200-row probe alone.
alternatives.reason: The probe tracked the official read to within 1 pp twice (0.085 vs 0.080; 0.540 vs 0.530), but it is held-out TRAIN data and the decision changes what is submitted, so the winner gets a real read under the locked protocol. The probe is used to pick the candidate cheaply, not to score it.

alternatives.option: Sweep temperature (0.3, 0.7) as well as greedy.
alternatives.reason: Each extra setting is another official read. Greedy is the single point most likely to win for a fine-tuned math model and it is the only one that also removes sampling variance from every future comparison in this session, which is worth more than a possible fraction of a point from an intermediate temperature.

alternatives.option: A second/third epoch over sft_v2 (the exp-02 data).
alternatives.reason: exp-03's sweep reads 0.680 / 0.670 / 0.670 greedy at steps 600 / 900 / 1112. The curve is flat, so that data is exhausted; more passes over it would buy nothing and cost the same hour.

alternatives.option: Add more off-policy data (MetaMathQA rendered directly, orca-math).
alternatives.reason: Off-policy chains are what exp-02 already did, and its residual is not a coverage problem. MetaMathQA's GSM problems are used here, but only as PROBLEMS - the chains come from the model itself, which is the part that is new.

alternatives.option: DPO/GRPO on the correct-vs-incorrect pairs the sampler produced.
alternatives.reason: Preference/RL training on top of this would need a reward loop, another set of hyperparameters and a second training run to debug, against 5.8 h left and an incumbent already packaged. Rejection sampling is the same signal (verified-correct chains) through the machinery that is already smoke-tested.

alternatives.option: Train on the RFT rows alone, without replay.
alternatives.reason: Every RFT row is on-policy and solvable-by-the-current-model, so training on them alone narrows the distribution exp-02 established and risks losing the 3541 problems the sampler never solved. 20000 rows of sft_v2 are mixed back in (33% of the file).

alternatives.option: Keep all 4 correct chains per problem.
alternatives.reason: That weights the easy problems hardest - the 8247 problems solved 4/4 would contribute twice as many rows as the 3892 solved 1/4, which is backwards. Capped at 2 per problem, shortest first, which also keeps the token bill at 41.5M.

alternatives.option: Just take an official greedy read of work/sft_v1/checkpoint-600 instead of training (WMA cheaper_variant).
alternatives.reason: Its probe lead over the final step is 0.680 vs 0.670 - two items on a set that is 97% train-seen. That is not a signal, and spending a 20 min official read to chase it would cost a third of the training run it is meant to replace. The checkpoints are on disk, so this stays available if exp-04 comes back flat.

alternatives.option: A uniform soup of checkpoints 600 / 900 / 1112 (WMA cheaper_variant).
alternatives.reason: Kept as the fallback if exp-04 is flat and time is short - it needs no training - but it is not tried first: the three checkpoints are ~600 steps apart in one cosine decay, so they are far more correlated than the independent runs soups usually average, and the expected effect is ~0.

alternatives.option: Continue training from work/sft_v1_greedy or from final_model.
alternatives.reason: transformers 4.57.3 GenerationConfig.save_pretrained rejects temperature 0.0 together with top_k -1, so a run started from a greedy-configured directory would train for an hour and then throw at the save. Training starts from work/sft_v1 (which still has the parent's sampling config) and the greedy fields are applied at package time by work/package_final.py --greedy.

alternatives.option: Stop at 0.670 and spend the remaining time on verification only.
alternatives.reason: final_model already holds 0.670 and is only overwritten if a candidate beats it under the same invocation, so the retry is free of downside risk. Verification is budgeted separately (~0.4 h) and still fits.

alternatives.option: Take an official read of an intermediate exp-04 checkpoint (350 / 525) instead of retraining.
alternatives.reason: It would sample the same wrong trajectory earlier - the direction exp-04 moved in is the problem, not the distance. Cheaper, but the best case is "less damage", not a gain.

alternatives.option: Select the LONGEST correct chain rather than the median.
alternatives.reason: Tempting because the failure was length collapse, but it over-corrects on one data point and the longest of 8 sampled chains is where the rambling and the redundant restatements are. Median restores the model's own length prior, which is the property exp-04 destroyed, without betting on the opposite extreme.

alternatives.option: Keep MetaMathQA problems in the pool (18000 of exp-04's 26054).
alternatives.reason: exp-04's own clean probe is the evidence against it: MetaMath-distribution items went UP 4.5 pp while GSM8K test went DOWN 4.5 pp. The pool here is GSM8K's own distribution - 7273 gsm8k-train problems plus the 781 OMI2 gsm8k problems not already in sft_v2.

alternatives.option: Change the learning rate or the replay size as well.
alternatives.reason: exp-04 is the control, and it differs from this run in the data file only (same parent, lr 5e-6, 1 epoch, token budget 20480, grad_accum 3, seed 0, 20000 replay rows). Moving one thing keeps the comparison interpretable in the time left. The replay count is the one exception - 20000 -> 30000 - because it is part of the same length fix, and it is recorded here rather than buried: exp-04 vs exp-05 is a data recipe comparison, not a clean single-variable ablation of chain selection.

alternatives.option: Leave it - the deliverable is already chosen and a variance number changes nothing that ships.
alternatives.reason: It changes what the session is entitled to claim. Two cards (exp-04, exp-05) were decided on paired splits of -9 and -5 against a bar of +6, and the same-weights repeat just produced -6. Without a variance estimate those verdicts are unfalsifiable assertions, and the next reader would inherit them as facts.

alternatives.option: A --limit 500 read instead, for a tighter estimate of the shipped model.
alternatives.reason: It answers a different question (sampling error over items) and would not isolate the run-to-run component at all, because a single n=500 read is still a single draw. It also costs ~45 min of the 2.5 h left and would not be comparable to any existing number, since the whole session is measured at n=200.

alternatives.option: Three more repeats for a proper variance estimate.
alternatives.reason: Each is ~20 min. One more gives three draws, which is enough to say whether 0.640 was an outlier or the 0.670 was, and to put a floor under the spread; the remaining time is better kept as margin for the final verification than spent narrowing an error bar that is already known to be non-zero.

alternatives.option: Swap final_model to exp-05's checkpoint now that 0.670 looks less solid.
alternatives.reason: The incumbent has two draws (0.670, 0.640) against the candidate's one (0.645), and it reasons 20% longer on a trend that predicts accuracy across three training runs. The evidence does not favour the swap, and swapping on noise is exactly the error this card exists to prevent.

alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and quote a published gemma-3-4b-pt GSM8K number
alternatives.reason: published numbers use a different prompt and decoder; rule 2 requires the comparator measured under THIS protocol

alternatives.option: Baseline at --limit 500 for a tighter CI
alternatives.reason: eval wall-clock scales with n and 150 is the harness default that every later card will reuse, so the comparator must be at 150

alternatives.option: --max-connections 8 to halve the wall-clock (the pre-verdict plan)
alternatives.reason: WMA e5 records 0.2733 -> 0.8533 on identical greedy weights from this parameter alone, with 99/150 outputs beginning '!!!!', plus EngineDeadError at 8/16. The probe below showed n=150 costs only ~13 min at the harness default 2, so the speed is not worth anchoring the whole batch to a possibly corrupted number. Frozen at 2 for every card.

alternatives.option: Force greedy decoding for the baseline by editing a copy of generation_config.json
alternatives.reason: the shipped sampling config (do_sample true, top_k 64, top_p 0.95) IS part of the starting checkpoint; changing it makes this a decode-config intervention rather than a baseline. Greedy is tested separately in a later card, against this comparator.

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full fine-tuning
alternatives.reason: the smoke run shows full FT of the 3.88B language model fits in 80 GB at 10.2k tok/s with fp32 masters + 8-bit Adam + Liger fused CE, so LoRA buys nothing here and full FT moves format/termination behaviour harder

alternatives.option: Train only on the 7473 native GSM8K train solutions
alternatives.reason: 7.5k short targets is enough to teach the stop token but not enough to move math ability; OpenMathInstruct-2 adds 60k GSM8K-derived chains at no extra wall-clock risk

alternatives.option: Prompt-engineering / decode-config fix only (stop strings, repetition penalty)
alternatives.reason: evaluate.py is immutable and exposes no stop-string flag, and the only decode knob that travels with the model is generation_config.json. That is a real lever but a separate, cheap card (planned exp-03) measured against a model that already terminates - it cannot fix format_ok 0.247 on its own.

alternatives.option: Train on the full 153k GSM8K-flavoured OpenMathInstruct-2 rows
alternatives.reason: 27.7M tokens/epoch already costs ~45 min; 2x that would take a third of the remaining budget before the first score, leaving no room for the RFT round that historically matters more

alternatives.option: Fewer/no few-shot-prefixed training rows
alternatives.reason: the grader ALWAYS prepends a 10-shot system message (~1700 tokens) while training rows are mostly zero-shot; 8% of rows carry a k in {2,3,4,10} prefix as insurance that the format survives the long prefix

alternatives.option: Leave the shipped sampling config alone and spend the 0.25 h on RFT instead
alternatives.reason: the two are not exclusive - RFT sampling for exp-04 is running on the GPU concurrently with this card's lock wait - and every later comparison inherits whichever decode regime the final model ships, so it should be settled before more training is stacked on top

alternatives.option: Sweep temperature (0.2 / 0.4) and repetition_penalty in the same card
alternatives.reason: each extra arm is another 13-min protocol read and another comparison at a 3-4 pp noise floor; greedy vs the shipped default is the one contrast with a mechanism behind it. If greedy wins, a temperature sweep is a follow-up card, not this one.

alternatives.option: Judge the decode regime from the private-dev number alone (0.7533 vs 0.6867)
alternatives.reason: those are different item sets AND different decoders; comparing them is exactly the comparator_protocol_mismatch pitfall. The greedy arm has to be measured under the frozen protocol on the same 150 items.

alternatives.option: Continue training from exp-02/epoch2 on the RFT rows only (1 epoch, low LR) instead of retraining from base
alternatives.reason: cheaper (~15 min) but it narrows the model onto 6748 train questions it already solves, and the corpus's own history is that RFT is retrained from base over the union; the budget affords the safer version

alternatives.option: Add the remaining ~78k unused augmented_gsm8k rows instead of RFT
alternatives.reason: more off-policy data of the same kind that produced the incumbent; the measured 26-point pass@4-minus-pass@1 gap says the binding constraint is trace reliability, not exposure to more problems

alternatives.option: GRPO / online RL from the incumbent
alternatives.reason: no verified GRPO path in this environment, and 6.4 h with an unclosed card is the wrong place to debug a new trainer; RFT captures most of the same signal offline

alternatives.option: Upweight RFT more than 2x, or train on RFT alone
alternatives.reason: 22.3k of 96.6k rows (23%) keeps the OpenMathInstruct-2 problem diversity that got the model to 0.75 in the first place; going further trades breadth for on-policy sharpness with no measurement to justify it

alternatives.option: Keep sampling to k=8 for better coverage of the 425 unsolved questions
alternatives.reason: coverage is already 94.1% at k=4 and the 425 residual questions keep their native GSM8K train solution in the mixture anyway; k=8 would have cost another ~20 min of GPU for the tail

alternatives.option: Ship the incumbent and stop
alternatives.reason: the soup costs no training at all - it was built on CPU while exp-04's eval ran - and its private-dev probe is the best number any candidate has produced; declining to measure it under the protocol would be leaving a free candidate unscored

alternatives.option: Judge the soup at the frozen n=150 like every previous card
alternatives.reason: exp-03 measured that protocol's read-to-read spread at +-4.7 pts by repeating it, and this card's expected effect is 2-5 pts. n=150 is structurally unable to answer the question; the previous cards' numbers stay valid at 150 and are reported, but the DECISION needs a larger n.

alternatives.option: A third eval repeat at n=150 instead of one read at n=500
alternatives.reason: three 150-item reads cost the same as one 500-item read and still only shrink the standard error by sqrt(3) on a set whose first-150 composition is itself a fixed idiosyncratic sample; 500 items is both tighter and less item-set-specific

alternatives.option: Weighted soup, or souping in exp-04/epoch1 as a third ingredient
alternatives.reason: exp-04/epoch1 is much weaker (dev-300 0.7067) and would drag the average; tuning soup weights on dev-300 with 300 items and a 2.5 pt binomial SE would be fitting noise. Uniform two-way is the version with no free parameters.

alternatives.option: A second RFT round from the soup
alternatives.reason: ~2 h of training against 4.4 h remaining and an unclosed card, on a line exp-04 just showed to be null. The remaining budget is better spent certifying which existing candidate to ship.

alternatives.option: Stop here and ship the verified two-way soup
alternatives.reason: this is the fallback and it stays live throughout - final_model/ already holds the greedy soup, CPU-load-checked and re-scored from a fresh process at 0.7467 (n=150). exp-06 only replaces it if the three-way beats it at n=500, so the downside is spent time, not a worse submission.

alternatives.option: Souping in exp-02/epoch1 or exp-04/epoch1 as the third ingredient (free, no training)

alternatives.option: Three epochs, or a larger corpus, to make ingredient C stronger than its predecessors
alternatives.reason: C does not need to be the best model, it needs to be a good model that fails differently; 2 epochs is the recipe already calibrated on this hardware (~1.55 h) and the budget has no room for more

alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and train immediately
alternatives.reason: every later card needs a comparator measured under the same protocol; without it a delta is unreadable

alternatives.option: Use a published gemma-3-4b-pt GSM8K number as the comparator
alternatives.reason: different prompt, template, decode settings and n; not the same protocol

alternatives.option: Run the full 1319-item test set
alternatives.reason: evaluate.py's own comment fixes --limit 150 as the intended protocol; full set costs ~9x the wall time

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full fine-tune
alternatives.reason: the deficit is behavioural (never stops, never formats) and large; full FT of the 3.88B text tower fits in 45 GB with liger fused CE, so there is no memory reason to take the LoRA capacity hit

alternatives.option: Train on openai/gsm8k train (7.5k) with its own '#### n' rationales
alternatives.reason: 10x less data, terse rationales, and '####' is a second answer marker the end-anchored scorer could pick up (pitfall double_answer_format)

alternatives.option: meta-math/MetaMathQA
alternatives.reason: same idea but a weaker teacher than OpenMathInstruct-2, and its bodies carry gsm8k's own '#### n' line - the exact double-marker pitfall

alternatives.option: Train only on gsm8k-sourced rows, no MATH rows
alternatives.reason: kept 12k augmented_math rows (17%) for arithmetic/algebra diversity; OpenMathInstruct-2's own ablations report MATH data does not hurt GSM8K

alternatives.option: Include the grader's own 10-shot prefix (fewshot_seed 42) in training prompts
alternatives.reason: that fits the harness's exact prefix rather than the format; instead 20% of rows carry a RANDOM 1-10 shot prefix drawn from the gsm8k TRAIN split, in inspect's own rendering, so the model is robust to any prefix

alternatives.option: 3+ epochs
alternatives.reason: 2 epochs is already 2.5 h of the 9.5 h left; a 3rd risks overfit and leaves no room for a follow-up card

alternatives.option: Evaluate the epoch-1 checkpoint while epoch 2 is still training (WMA cheaper_variant 2)
alternatives.reason: training peaks at 44.7 GB of 80 GB and the dev protocol asks vLLM for 0.85; running both would either OOM or change the protocol, and a comparator measured under a different protocol is not a comparator

alternatives.option: Stop at 1 epoch (WMA cheaper_variant 4)
alternatives.reason: the checkpoint ladder below makes epoch 1 recoverable at zero extra cost, so the second epoch is bought and not committed to

alternatives.option: Pass --temperature to evaluate.py
alternatives.reason: evaluate.py has no such flag and rule 5 forbids modifying it; the only lever the harness leaves open is the served checkpoint's own generation_config.json

alternatives.option: temperature 0.7 or 0.3 instead of 0.0
alternatives.reason: a sweep costs one eval per point and the mechanism (a single graded sample, end-anchored scorer) makes the argmax path strictly the right target; if greedy loses, the sweep is the follow-up

alternatives.option: Leave the decode alone and spend the slot on RFT
alternatives.reason: not exclusive - this card costs one 5-minute eval and its answer changes which checkpoint RFT should start from and how every later delta is read

alternatives.option: A third epoch on sft_v1 (the OpenMathInstruct mixture)
alternatives.reason: off-policy and already twice-seen; exp-02's ladder shows the gain came late in epoch 2, not from more passes over the same teacher text

alternatives.option: Pull more OpenMathInstruct-2 rows from the full 14M train split
alternatives.reason: another 2.5 h of training for off-policy data, and only 5.5 h are left including the final assembly and verification

alternatives.option: DPO / GRPO on correct-vs-incorrect samples
alternatives.reason: the sampled pairs exist, but neither trainer is set up here and a preference run inside 5.5 h with no smoke history is how a batch ends with nothing shippable

alternatives.option: Pure RFT with no replay
alternatives.reason: 20k rows all derived from 7473 questions, 2 epochs, would narrow the model onto the gsm8k train distribution; 20k rows of sft_v1 are mixed back in at 50% to hold the OpenMathInstruct behaviour

alternatives.option: Add gold gsm8k-train rationales for the 395 unsolved questions
alternatives.reason: 395 rows (1% of the mixture) in a terse style unlike everything else the model has been trained on; not worth the second format

alternatives.option: Re-sample the same 7473 gsm8k TRAIN questions again
alternatives.reason: exp-04 already trained on 20013 rows drawn from them for 2 epochs; a second pass over the same questions is the narrowing failure mode the corpus attributes to rft, and the new samples would be near-copies of the training targets

alternatives.option: Plain SFT on the teacher solutions for the same 24000 unseen problems
alternatives.reason: off-policy; the round that worked here put the model's own correct chains back into it, and the verified-sample filter is what makes the targets trustworthy

alternatives.option: 2 epochs, as exp-04 used
alternatives.reason: 2.6 h are left and the run must still be scored on the full 1319-item split (30 min) and packaged; 1 epoch over 40000 rows is ~45 min and fits with margin

alternatives.option: A weight soup of exp-02/final and exp-04/final
alternatives.reason: cheap, but the two are 3 points apart on the full split and the cheaper lever does not use the 41047 verified rows already generated and paid for

alternatives.option: Stop here and ship exp-04
alternatives.reason: final_model/ already holds exp-04/final and is verified; this card is upside-only and SHIPPING_RULE.md forbids replacing it on anything short of a full-split win

alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and start SFT immediately
alternatives.reason: every later card needs a comparator scored under the same protocol; without it no delta is interpretable

alternatives.option: Baseline at --limit 1319 (full test set)
alternatives.reason: ~9x the wall clock; --limit 150 is the harness default and is what all later cards will use

alternatives.option: Greedy-decode read of the base checkpoint (rewrite generation_config, re-eval) to attribute the later gain between decode and training
alternatives.reason: exp-01 shows the loss is non-termination, which greedy does not fix; ~0.15 h of GPU for an attribution number about a checkpoint that will never be shipped. do_sample:false is written into the trained checkpoint regardless.

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full fine-tuning
alternatives.reason: the required behaviour change (stop after the answer, adopt a solution style) is a large distribution shift from a pretrained-only checkpoint; the smoke run shows full FT of the 3.88B text decoder fits in 80 GB and runs an epoch in ~1.2 h, so there is no budget reason to accept LoRA's capacity ceiling.

alternatives.option: MetaMathQA (395k) as the corpus
alternatives.reason: its bodies carry gsm8k's own '#### N' line, which is a second answer marker next to the required 'ANSWER: N' (pitfall double_answer_format). OpenMathInstruct-2 solutions carry only \boxed{}, which is removed cleanly.

alternatives.option: Train the full 2.57M gsm-type rows of OpenMathInstruct-2
alternatives.reason: ~1.4 B tokens, far past the 9.65 h left. Capped at <=4 solutions per original-gsm8k problem and 1 per augmented problem: 101 262 rows, 54 M tokens, ~1.6 h.

alternatives.option: Two epochs in this run instead of one
alternatives.reason: 3.1 h against the 9.2 h left, and the epoch-1 checkpoint would sit mid-cosine so it would not be a fair read of one epoch. Held back as an exp-03 candidate to be chosen against 'more solutions per problem' on this card's evidence.

alternatives.option: Second epoch over the same data/sft_pool.jsonl
alternatives.reason: OpenMathInstruct-2 has 2.57M gsm-type rows and exp-02 used 4% of them, so unseen solutions are available where re-reading seen ones mostly buys memorisation of the same 101k targets.

alternatives.option: Rejection-sampling fine-tuning (sample from exp-02, keep correct, retrain)
alternatives.reason: sampling k=4 over ~30k problems plus filtering plus training does not fit the 7.35 h left beside an eval budget, and the corpus-size curve says plain SFT data has not run out yet. Kept as the exp-04 line if this card flattens.

alternatives.option: GSM-only corpus of further OpenMathInstruct-2 solutions (the first version of this card, data/sft_pool_v3.jsonl)
alternatives.reason: the exp-03 WMA verdict's probe p2 showed 0 of its 110 000 augmented rows sit on problems exp-02 had not already seen, and re-running the extraction confirmed why: the whole gsm+augmented_gsm8k slice of OpenMathInstruct-2 contains only 81 069 distinct problems (2.57 M rows at ~32 solutions each), all of which exp-02 covered. That corpus could only have tested solution diversity, which the verdict priced at [-0.03, +0.04]. v3 is kept on disk but not used.

alternatives.option: Reject the math / augmented_math subsets on format grounds
alternatives.reason: the earlier draft of this card rejected them because MATH answers are LaTeX. Filtering expected_answer to a plain integer removes that objection entirely and leaves 7.29 M rows over 323 381 distinct problems - the only large source of problems this model has genuinely never seen. Capped at 1 solution per problem and 34 000 rows so GSM-style stays the majority.

alternatives.option: MetaMathQA for the new problems instead
alternatives.reason: its bodies carry gsm8k's own '#### N' line, a second answer marker beside the required one (pitfall double_answer_format), and it is GPT-3.5-generated where OpenMathInstruct-2 is 405B-generated. The integer-answer MATH slice gives new problems from the corpus already downloaded and already validated by exp-02.

alternatives.option: Train from the base checkpoint on all 240k rows under one cosine schedule
alternatives.reason: cleaner schedule, but it discards exp-02's 1.59 h and leaves no fallback if it lands lower. Continuing keeps 0.720 on disk.

alternatives.option: 150 339 rows (60 000 MATH + 62 000 augmented-gsm8k + 28 339 gsm8k)
alternatives.reason: measured at 102.9 M tokens = ~2.9 h against the 7.0 h left, which would leave no room for a follow-up card. Trimmed to 114 339 rows / 74.9 M tokens / ~2.1 h.

alternatives.option: Raise the few-shot share above 20% to match the grader's always-10-shot prompt
alternatives.reason: measured, not assumed: exp-02 scores 0.710 on the held-out 300 with the grader's exact 10-shot prefix and 0.700 with none. There is no prefix-sensitivity left to buy, so the share stays at 20%.

alternatives.option: A third SFT stage on ~110k further rows
alternatives.reason: 2.1 h of the 4.4 h left for an effect exp-03 measured at ~+1.5 pp inside the noise band, and it would leave no room to verify the submission. The soup costs ~0.4 h.

alternatives.option: Rejection-sampling fine-tuning on the model's own correct samples
alternatives.reason: generation over ~20k problems plus filtering plus a training stage plus an eval does not fit 4.4 h with the verification budget reserved, and a failed attempt would burn the margin that protects final_model.

alternatives.option: Ship exp-03 without trying the soup
alternatives.reason: exp-03's own lead is inside the noise band, so a cheap third candidate scored under the same protocol is worth 0.4 h; if it loses, exp-03 still ships.

alternatives.option: Soup exp-03's own checkpoint-300/600/888 instead
alternatives.reason: those three are ~0.3 epochs apart on one cosine annealing to zero, so they are far more correlated than exp-02/final and exp-03/final, which are separated by a full 114k-row stage. Less diversity to average over.

alternatives.option: Search alpha over {0.25, 0.5, 0.75}
alternatives.reason: each alpha costs a full n=500 read (~9 min) plus a held-out read; with 4.4 h left and verification reserved, one principled midpoint is scored rather than a sweep whose winner would be selected on noise.

alternatives.option: Stop and ship exp-03
alternatives.reason: final_model/ already holds exp-03 and is verified, so the remaining 3.9 h are otherwise idle. This card cannot lower the submission - it only replaces it if it wins on the pooled read.

alternatives.option: Alpha sweep around the exp-04 soup
alternatives.reason: the soup lost to BOTH ingredients at n=500, so the interpolation path is not merely mis-tuned; a sweep would be selecting on noise along a line that is already below the endpoints.

alternatives.option: Retrain from base on the union of v1+v4 in one clean cosine
alternatives.reason: 215k rows is ~3.3 h, over budget, and it would discard 3.6 h of accumulated training for an untested schedule argument.

alternatives.option: Rejection-sampling fine-tuning
alternatives.reason: still does not fit: generation, filtering, training and evaluation inside 3.9 h with a 1 h safety margin reserved for finalisation.

alternatives.option: Sweep ckpts/exp-03/checkpoint-300 and -600 on the held-out 300 before launching (the exp-05 verdict's tier-3 suggestion)
alternatives.reason: 0.25 h of the 3.8 h left, and the identical sweep on exp-02's trajectory was monotone (0.690 / 0.7033 / 0.710 at steps 400 / 600 / 789). exp-03 has the same one-epoch cosine-to-zero shape at half the lr, so an interior checkpoint beating the annealed endpoint is unlikely, and the 0.25 h is worth more as end-of-session margin. Recorded as a knowingly skipped check.

alternatives.option: 104 000 rows (the first v5 build)
alternatives.reason: measured at 70.1 M tokens = ~1.97 h, which left under 1 h of end-of-session margin. Trimmed to 92 000 rows / ~1.75 h.

alternatives.reason: they would be on their third epoch while everything else is on its first; halved to 14 000 to keep the GSM8K style anchor without pushing 7 129 problems toward memorisation.

alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and compare a post-trained model against a published gemma-3-4b-pt GSM8K number
alternatives.reason: a number from a different harness/prompt is not a comparator under this protocol (pitfall comparator_protocol_mismatch)

alternatives.option: Baseline at --limit 500 for a tighter CI
alternatives.reason: ~3x the wall clock and every later card would have to match it; 150 is the harness default and the protocol I will keep throughout

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full fine-tuning
alternatives.reason: the base has never been instruction-tuned, so the change needed spans the whole distribution; a full FT fits in 80 GB at bs 8 with 8-bit Adam (measured in the smoke runs below)

alternatives.option: Train only on the 7.5k GSM8K train split
alternatives.reason: 7.5k terse human solutions is thin for a 4B and their calculator-annotation style is not what I want emitted; OpenMathInstruct-2 adds 45k same-domain problems

alternatives.option: Add OpenMathInstruct-2's MATH-family rows for breadth
alternatives.reason: heavy LaTeX would pull the answer style away from the plain prose the numeric matcher reads; keep the first corpus tight

alternatives.option: Re-score the frozen base greedily for a decode-matched comparator (WMA cheaper_variant 1)
alternatives.reason: ~10 min GPU plus a card and a 20 min lock wait; the expected effect here is an order of magnitude larger than the decode difference, and every later card-to-card comparison is greedy-vs-greedy anyway. The base number therefore stays a sampled read and is labelled as such

alternatives.option: liger-kernel fused linear cross-entropy to cut the 262k-vocab logit memory
alternatives.reason: the container root filesystem is a full 64 MB overlay, the wheel could not install; removed the half-installed package

alternatives.option: Continue training exp-02/final on the RFT data alone at a lower LR
alternatives.reason: cheaper (~25 min) but it trains a second time on questions the model has already fitted and risks collapsing onto its own phrasing; the standard RFT recipe (Yuan et al.) retrains the base on SFT union RFT and keeps the off-policy diversity

alternatives.option: Scale the off-policy corpus instead (data/sft_v2.jsonl, 77.5k rows, 25k more unique problems, already built and contamination-checked)
alternatives.reason: the ckpt-800 = final result says another pass over more of the same 405B-generated solutions is the weaker lever; sft_v2 is kept as the exp-04 fallback if RFT does not move the number

alternatives.option: DPO/GRPO on correct-vs-incorrect samples
alternatives.reason: no preference-pair pipeline exists here and a GRPO loop would not fit the remaining 7 h alongside a final eval; RFT extracts most of the same signal from the samples already drawn

alternatives.option: A second RFT round from exp-03/final (hard-question pool at k=16 already built at data/rft_pool_hard.jsonl, 2345 items)
alternatives.reason: the first round's mechanism was contradicted by the n=250 read, so paying 0.6 h of sampling plus 1.6 h of training to iterate it is the worse bet with 5.4 h left

alternatives.option: Raise the learning rate to 2e-5 or run 2 epochs
alternatives.reason: exp-02 already showed the score flat between step 800 and step 1632 at 1e-5, so the schedule is not what is binding; and an LR change cannot be attributed alongside the data change

alternatives.option: Stop training and spend the remaining time on tighter measurement only
alternatives.reason: the limit-500 finalist re-score is planned as exp-05 regardless; a 1.6 h run still fits in front of it with ~2 h of slack, and 25k more unique problems is the last untried data axis

alternatives.option: Submit exp-04 on the dev-150 reading alone and spend the remaining time on a fifth training run
alternatives.reason: no training that fits in 3.3 h could be measured well enough to be adopted, and getting the checkpoint choice right is worth more than an unmeasurable increment

alternatives.option: Break the tie with the n=250 train-split watch set only (exp-04 0.692 vs exp-03 0.636)
alternatives.reason: free and already done, but it is zero-shot GSM8K-train text and the WMA notes 76 of its 250 items share >=60% of their rare words with some training question, so it flatters coverage-type changes like exp-04's

alternatives.option: --limit 1319 (the whole test split) on both
alternatives.reason: ~3x the wall clock of limit-500 per candidate; at n=500 the standard error is already ~2 points, enough to resolve a 1.3-point question

alternatives.option: A fifth training run in the remaining 2.8 h
alternatives.reason: 1.5-1.9 h of training plus an n=500 read would leave no slack for packaging, and the result would land on the same unresolvable ruler

alternatives.option: Ensembling the two models at decode time (majority vote)

alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and use published gemma-3-4b-pt GSM8K numbers
alternatives.reason: a number from a different harness/prompt/limit is not a comparator under this protocol

alternatives.reason: eval throughput is still unknown; 150 is the harness default and keeps every later card comparable at low cost

alternatives.option: --max-connections 16 for speed (as first locked)

alternatives.option: Pin temperature 0 on the base snapshot to get a greedy comparator
alternatives.reason: the starting revision must stay immutable this batch. The base is measured under its own shipped decode (do_sample true, top_k 64, top_p 0.95, temperature unset -> vLLM samples at T=1); a separate later card measures the greedy-vs-sampling effect on a trained checkpoint, where the generation_config is mine to set.

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full-parameter SFT
alternatives.reason: an 80 GB H100 and a 4B model leave room for full FT (measured 35 GB peak at bs 8 with the Liger fused CE); full FT is the stronger baseline and avoids the adapter/merge failure mode in pitfalls.yaml (final_model_not_loadable)

alternatives.option: Render every training row with the grader's 10-shot system prefix
alternatives.reason: the prefix is 2044 tokens against a 167-token target, so it would cost ~4x the compute per row; 12% of rows carry it, which exposes the model to the graded rendering without paying for it on every row

alternatives.option: RFT / self-distillation first
alternatives.reason: there is no fine-tuned checkpoint to sample from yet; RFT is the natural next card once this one lands

alternatives.option: WMA cheaper variant: pilot the same recipe on a 15k-row subset (~25 min) before committing the full epoch
alternatives.reason: the pilot's information is 'does the recipe work at all', which the verdict already puts at L0 0.92 / L1 0.88 / L2 higher [0.30, 0.65]; the ~45 min it would cost (pilot + eval + its own card and lock) is better spent on the full epoch plus a targeted follow-up. The residual risk it would have covered - train/eval rendering mismatch - is instead covered by save_steps checkpoints and by a probe-set read under the graded 10-shot rendering.

alternatives.option: Raise the 10-shot fraction above 12% because of history/r-94f796fd (0.10 plain vs 0.52 eval-rendered on SmolLM3)
alternatives.reason: that precedent's 'plain' arm used a different prompt entirely; here 100% of rows already use the grader's exact user template and templates/gemma3.jinja, and only the 2044-token system prefix varies. 11.7k rows do carry it. Raising the fraction would multiply epoch cost by ~2-4x for a mismatch that is one message deep.

alternatives.option: Leave the checkpoint on the base decode and spend the time on more training instead
alternatives.reason: one eval (~8 min, no training) against a lever a same-protocol precedent measured at +20.6 points (history/r-a3f23d29/exp-02: 0.627 -> 0.833 at n=150); no training change comes close to that per minute

alternatives.option: Ask evaluate.py for temperature 0
alternatives.reason: evaluate.py must not be modified (task rule 5) and it sends no temperature at all; the only place the decode can be set is the checkpoint's own generation_config.json, which vLLM loads as the server's default sampling params

alternatives.option: Copy the checkpoint to set the new config
alternatives.reason: 8.6 GB and ~1 min per variant for a two-field JSON change; make_variant.py symlinks the weights and rewrites only generation_config.json, so both arms are provably the same weights

alternatives.option: Rejection-sampling fine-tuning on the incumbent's own correct samples (the original plan for this card)
alternatives.reason: ABANDONED ON MEASURED COST, not on principle. Two sampling passes were run and killed. Zero-shot, k=4 over 20173 problems: 1.15 h, solve rate only 0.38 and mean generation 421 tokens against ~200 in the graded read - without the 10-shot prefix the model rambles into the 512-token cap, so most samples were rejected for finish_reason != stop, and the 9654 rows that survived are biased to the easy tail (kept at data/rft_v0_zeroshot.jsonl). Re-sampling under the grader's 10-shot prefix fixed the regime (prefix caching gave 20.8k input tok/s) but decode slowed to 9.4 generations/s because each sequence now carries a 2157-token KV, projecting 2.27 h for the same 76692 generations. With 5.15 h left that is over half the remaining budget for a +1 to +5 lever, against ~1.4 h for this card.

alternatives.option: Repeat a second epoch over the stage-1 file
alternatives.reason: the model has already fitted those exact 97173 rows; the 185034-row pool at max_per_problem 4 contains 95034 pairs it has never seen, which is strictly more informative for the same compute

alternatives.option: Checkpoint sweep of checkpoint-1520 / 2280 under greedy (C5)
alternatives.reason: cheap (~10 min) but this was a single cosine-annealed epoch, so the final checkpoint is the annealed one and a mid-schedule checkpoint is both less trained and at a higher LR; kept as a fallback card if this one fails or if time runs short

alternatives.option: DPO on correct/incorrect sample pairs
alternatives.reason: the sampling pass produces the pairs for free, but DPO needs its own hyperparameter search and a reference model in memory; with ~5 h left, one well-understood method beats two half-tuned ones

alternatives.option: 70000 fresh rows rather than all 95034
alternatives.reason: measured stage-1 throughput was 14.8 samples/s, so 70000 rows is ~1.31 h and fits the remaining budget with room for the evaluation, the checkpoint selection and the packaging; the 25034 rows left on the table are recorded here rather than passed off as full coverage

alternatives.option: Pick by the pooled 450-item total (0.7556 vs 0.7378) and skip the extra reads
alternatives.reason: the two components are measured on different distributions (GSM8K test items vs held-out GSM8K train items), so pooling weights a train-distribution proxy equally with the graded one; 30 min of GPU buys a direct answer instead of an argument about how to average

alternatives.option: Keep the incumbent because its dev-150 number is higher
alternatives.reason: 0.7200 vs 0.7133 is a one-item difference at n=150 with stderr 0.037; treating that as a result is exactly what the protocol's comparator rule exists to prevent

alternatives.option: Train something else with the remaining 3.4 h
alternatives.reason: another stage plus its evaluation does not fit alongside the packaging and CPU verification still to do, and exp-04 just measured the marginal value of more off-policy rows at roughly zero. Deciding correctly between two finished candidates is worth more than a third rushed one.

alternatives.option: --limit 1319 (the full test split) for both arms
alternatives.reason: ~35 min per arm at the measured throughput; n=500 brings stderr to ~0.02, enough to separate a 2-3 point gap, and leaves margin for packaging and verification before the deadline

alternatives.option: A third supervised stage on the 25034 fresh rows left over
alternatives.reason: exp-04 measured the marginal value of 70000 more off-policy rows at +1.6 points and not separable from zero; 25000 more is a smaller version of a lever already measured near-null, and it would not leave room to evaluate and repackage safely

alternatives.option: Rejection-sampling fine-tuning, revisited
alternatives.reason: measured at ~2.3 h for sampling alone under the 10-shot prefix (exp-04 situation); it does not fit in 2.85 h with training, evaluation and repackaging still to come

alternatives.option: Spend the time on a --limit 1319 read of final_model instead
alternatives.reason: it would tighten the estimate but cannot raise the score; a lever that might raise it is worth more, and the 1319 read is what to do with whatever time is left afterwards

alternatives.reason: that is a hyperparameter sweep and each point costs a 13-min read; an equal average is the standard soup and the only point that can be tested and acted on inside the remaining budget

alternatives.option: Stop here and submit final_model at 0.754
alternatives.reason: safe, but it leaves 2.5 h of an H100 idle on a task whose objective is maximum accuracy, and it leaves the one open question of the session answered by a tie-break rule instead of a measurement

alternatives.option: Another training stage
alternatives.reason: does not fit: the shortest stage this session was 1.30 h of training plus 0.25 h of evaluation, and exp-04 measured that lever at not-separable-from-zero

alternatives.reason: both arms are greedy, so a repeat is not an independent draw - it would only re-measure vLLM batching nondeterminism, which is already bounded at ~2 items by final_model reading 0.754 against exp-04-greedy's 0.750 on byte-identical weights
