alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and train first
alternatives.reason: Rule 2 of the protocol: every later card needs a comparator measured under the identical protocol. Without it no delta is interpretable.

alternatives.option: Use --limit 150 (the evaluate.py default)
alternatives.reason: 200 items halves the binomial stderr per point (~3.5pp -> ~3.2pp) at ~30% more wall clock; cheap at this stage and used for every later card.

alternatives.option: Hold out part of the GSM8K train split as the dev set instead of the official test prefix
alternatives.reason: The grading pipeline (10-shot system prompt, vLLM server, match scorer) is only reproduced faithfully by evaluate.py itself; a hand-rolled dev loop would measure a different thing. Train-split holdout is still used to filter training data, not to select checkpoints.

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full fine-tuning
alternatives.reason: The gap to close is tens of points from a raw pretrained checkpoint that has never seen an instruction format; this is a capability+format change, not a style nudge. Memory is not the constraint (full FT of the 3.88B language model fits in 80GB with the selected-token loss below), so the usual reason to reach for LoRA does not apply.

alternatives.option: Train on the GSM8K train split alone (7473 rows)
alternatives.reason: Its reference solutions are two or three terse lines with calculator annotations; 7.5k rows of that is thin for a full fine-tune. It is kept as 8% of the mixture for exact style coverage, with OpenMathInstruct-2's longer worked solutions as the bulk.

alternatives.option: Render every training row with the grader's 10-shot prefix
alternatives.reason: Measured: a few-shot row is 2384 tokens against 334 for a zero-shot row, so all-few-shot would be a 7x compute bill for the same 97k problems. 8% of rows carry the exact 10-shot prefix as robustness insurance; the rest are zero-shot.

alternatives.option: Fixed per-device batch size
alternatives.reason: Smoke run 1 OOMed in the cross-entropy: gemma-3's vocabulary is 262144, so a batch of 8x3328 tokens needs a 16.8 GiB logits allocation. Replaced with a token-budget batcher plus a loss that only runs lm_head on label!=-100 positions.

alternatives.option: liger-kernel fused linear cross-entropy for speed
alternatives.reason: Installed and immediately uninstalled: the container's root overlay is 64 MB and 100% full, so the wheel unpacked truncated (OSError errno 28 on import). Not worth fighting for; the selective loss already solves the memory problem.

alternatives.option: Retrain from the base snapshot on the whole union (158186 rows, ~2.1 h) -- this card's original plan
alternatives.reason: Changed after the exp-03 WMA verdict. It retrieved a near-controlled precedent (/history/r-d2611dd8) that ran the same RFT mixture both ways on a comparable base model: warm-started from the SFT checkpoint it scored 0.716 at n=500, from the base snapshot 0.596 -- 12 points worse from base. Its 16 completed rft-family cards cluster in [-0.047, +0.027] with a median near -0.01, and it put this card's from-base delta at [-0.02, +0.06], i.e. inside the protocol's own noise. The warm-start arm costs a third of the time and is the arm the precedent favours, so it is run first; the from-base arm remains available with the 158186-row corpus (data/sft_v2.jsonl, already built and contamination-checked) if this one disappoints.

alternatives.option: A second epoch over the same 97k rows of exp-02
alternatives.reason: exp-02's loss was still drifting down (0.35 -> 0.33) with no sign of overfitting, so extra optimisation is not the binding constraint; unique problems are. The 30k unseen OMI rows plus 30.7k self-samples are new signal, and rows exp-02 has already seen are excluded from this corpus by an exact (prompt, target) set difference.

alternatives.option: Score exp-02's checkpoint-350/700/1050, which exist and were never evaluated (the verdict's cheapest suggestion, ~25 min of GPU)
alternatives.reason: Deferred, not dismissed. Checkpoint selection pays when a run overfits, and exp-02 shows the opposite signature: a single epoch, a cosine schedule that had decayed lr to near zero by the end, and a loss still falling (0.35 at step 225 -> 0.33 at step 1110) with no eval-side degradation. checkpoint-350 and -700 sit mid-schedule at lr 8.0e-6 and ~4.4e-6 and are strictly undertrained on the same data. The checkpoints are kept, so this stays available if the remaining budget goes unused; spending 25 min of GPU on it now would come out of the only run that can produce a better final_model.

alternatives.option: Rejection-sample with a larger k, or from the harder tail only
alternatives.reason: k=4 over 20000 problems already took 28 min of GPU and returned 30713 usable rows after answer-matching and chain dedup. Raising k mostly returns more copies of problems the model already solves; the failure mode RFT does not fix is the 15.75% of problems no sample got right, and no amount of self-sampling reaches those.

alternatives.option: Keep the few-shot share at 8%
alternatives.reason: Kept at the 6% the merged corpus was built with: a few-shot row costs 2384 tokens against 334 zero-shot, and exp-02 showed the format transferred to the grader's 10-shot prompt perfectly (99% ANSWER: lines, 1% truncation) with only 8%. 6% of 158k rows is still 9.5k few-shot rows, more than exp-02 had in absolute terms.

alternatives.option: Raise max-per-problem on OpenMathInstruct-2 from 2 to 4 (~150k more rows, same problems)
alternatives.reason: Extra chains for problems the model already fits is the weakest kind of new data; exp-03 already added 30713 self-generated chains for 16850 of those same problems and the delta was not resolvable. New problems are the binding constraint, not new chains.

alternatives.option: A second rejection-sampling round from exp-03
alternatives.reason: RFT round 2 costs ~0.5 h of sampling for a distribution the model already covers -- exp-02's pass@4 was 0.8425, so round 2 mostly re-collects solved problems. It also cannot touch the ~16% of problems no sample solves, which is where the residual failures live.

alternatives.option: meta-math/MetaMathQA as the new source
alternatives.reason: It is another augmentation of the same GSM8K train problems, so it inherits the same problem set that is already exhausted, and its 'The answer is: X' ending is a second answer marker that has to be stripped (the double_answer_format pitfall). orca-math is 200k genuinely distinct grade-school word problems from a different generator.

alternatives.option: Retrain from the base snapshot on everything (the arm deferred in exp-03)
alternatives.reason: Still deferred, for the reason the exp-03 verdict gave: its one near-controlled precedent has the from-base arm 12 points below the warm-start arm, and at ~2.5 h for the union corpus it would consume most of what is left. The warm-start arm has now produced the incumbent twice.

alternatives.option: Keep exp-03's 5e-6 learning rate so the corpus is the only change
alternatives.reason: Given up deliberately, and it costs this card the clean single-variable read. The exp-04 verdict retrieved /history/r-2fa3e9e7/exp-02, which lost 6.7 points continuing on orca-math at exactly 5e-6 and whose successor card blamed the rate, and /history/r-5720f98a/exp-13, which used 1e-6 for a 199k-row orca continuation. This corpus is also 80% off-distribution prose. 3e-6 is the compromise; the confound is recorded here rather than discovered later.

alternatives.option: Filter orca-math answers with a model-based verifier instead of a positional heuristic
alternatives.reason: No gold answers exist for orca-math, so a verifier would be checking the model against itself. The positional filter (final number must lie in the last 140 characters, plain numeric, no competing marker) rejected 4276 of 99276 candidate rows and is the same last-number rule the grader applies, so a row that passes it is a row whose label the grader would also read.

alternatives.option: Ship exp-04 because it has the highest n=200 number and stop
alternatives.reason: 0.740 vs 0.730 is 2 items out of 200 net. The estimator put exp-04's effect at flat [-0.06, +0.03] and the paired test gives p=0.856; choosing on that is choosing on noise, and it is the failure mode this whole session's protocol exists to prevent.

alternatives.option: One more training run in the remaining 3.9 h
alternatives.reason: Each of the last two runs bought a delta the measurement cannot resolve, so a third would most likely add a fourth indistinguishable candidate rather than a better model. The cheaper win now is to find out which of the three I already have is actually best -- 6.6x the evaluation items for about 8 minutes each.

alternatives.option: n=500 rather than the full 1319
alternatives.reason: The whole test set costs about 8 minutes per candidate at the measured throughput, against about 5 for n=500. There is no reason to take the smaller sample; 1319 items put the binomial stderr near 1.2pp instead of 2.0pp at n=500 and 3.2pp at n=200.

alternatives.option: Drop exp-02 from the sweep to save about 8 minutes (the verdict's cheaper variant)
alternatives.reason: Kept. Its n=200 discordant split against exp-04 does project to a clear win for exp-04, but exp-02 is the only candidate whose corpus is disjoint from the other two's late additions, so it is the one arm that would catch a systematic regression across the whole warm-start chain. It also has to be re-scored here regardless: comparing a 1319-item number against its stored 200-item first-N read would be the invocation-mismatch trap.

alternatives.option: Also sweep exp-04's checkpoint-900/1200/1500 in this card
alternatives.reason: Held in reserve. Four candidates is what the card can score and interpret in one pass; if the full-test read leaves the top two within a paired-test tie, the kept checkpoints are the next thing to score with the time that is left.

alternatives.option: Another training run in the remaining 3.3 h
alternatives.reason: exp-05 just showed that the last training run made the model worse and that the protocol used to steer it could not tell. A fifth checkpoint costs 1.5 h and would be chosen on the same instrument that already misranked one. Averaging and checkpoint selection cost minutes and are the two levers that operate inside the gap the failure actually opened.

alternatives.option: Sweep exp-03's checkpoint-250/500 as well
alternatives.reason: Those are earlier than exp-03/final on a trajectory whose endpoint is the best single checkpoint measured, so they are undertrained rather than mid-gap. exp-04's checkpoint-1200 is the earliest surviving point between the two endpoints of the run that overshot.

alternatives.option: Score more soup mixing ratios (0.5/0.5 is already in, adding 0.6, 0.8, 0.9)
alternatives.reason: Selection pressure. Four candidates already sit within 1.2pp of each other and 1319 items give about 1.2pp of stderr, so the more near-identical arms are scored, the more the winner is the luckiest rather than the best. Three new arms, and a pre-declared paired-test bar to beat, is the limit this instrument supports.

alternatives.option: Pick whichever candidate scores highest and ship it
alternatives.reason: That is what the n=200 protocol would have done in exp-05, and it would have shipped a model 14 items worse. The decision rule below requires the challenger to WIN the paired test against the incumbent, not merely to out-score it.

alternatives.option: Ship soup234 now because it has the highest number
alternatives.reason: It is the move exp-05 proved wrong at n=200, one level up. exp-06's decision rule asked for p<0.05 and got p=0.520, and its null arm says 7.2% of items flip between weight sets this close. Adopting on that would be adopting on an unreplicated read.

alternatives.option: Keep soup34 and stop, since the challenger did not clear the pre-declared bar
alternatives.reason: That is the letter of exp-06's rule and it would be defensible, but the rule exists to stop noise-chasing, not to protect an arbitrary incumbent: soup34 itself only became incumbent by a p=1.000 tie with exp-03. With 2.8 h left and a replication costing 10 minutes, refusing to look is a worse use of the budget than looking.

alternatives.option: Replicate all six candidates
alternatives.reason: Only two are live. exp-03 (0.6990) and soup37 (0.7013) are within a point of both, but neither leads, and adding arms is what makes a max-of-k choice unreliable in the first place. Two arms, two extra reads.

alternatives.option: Score a wider set of soup ratios or a fourth-model soup
alternatives.reason: There is no fourth independent model -- exp-03 and exp-04 are a chain, exp-02 is their ancestor -- and exp-06 already showed the 0.5 and 0.7 mixes and the three-way land within half a point of each other. More ratios is more selection pressure on the same instrument.

alternatives.option: Rely on the CPU load check package_model.py already does

alternatives.option: Re-run at --limit 1319 with default concurrency

alternatives.option: Spend the remaining time on another soup ratio or another training run

Another arm would add selection pressure, not accuracy. An unverified deliverable is the only remaining risk that is large rather than marginal.

alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and use a published gemma-3-4b-pt GSM8K number
alternatives.reason: published numbers use a different prompt and scorer; protocol rule 2 requires the comparator be measured under this exact protocol

alternatives.option: Baseline at --limit 50 to save time
alternatives.reason: grading uses --limit 150; a 50-item number is not a comparator for later 150-item cards

alternatives.option: Prompt/decode-only fix (stop strings, lower max-tokens)
alternatives.reason: evaluate.py and templates/ are immutable and the task passes no stop-string; the only lever inside the model artifact is training it to emit <end_of_turn>, so a decode-only card cannot fix the 80% of responses that never terminate

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full fine-tune
alternatives.reason: the base checkpoint must learn a turn-termination behaviour it has never produced, not just a style; full FT of the 3.88B text tower fits in 80 GB at a 8192-token micro-batch budget (measured), so there is no memory reason to accept LoRA's capacity limit

alternatives.option: Train only on the 7.5k original gsm8k train solutions
alternatives.reason: 7.5k rows is ~4M tokens; OpenMathInstruct-2's gsm8k-train-derived augmentations add 150k more solutions in the same domain at no contamination cost (checker: 0 matches over all 59946 rows)

alternatives.option: Train zero-shot only (no k-shot prefix rows)
alternatives.reason: the grader always prepends a 2184-token 10-shot block; 22% of rows carry a random 2-10-shot prefix so the trained behaviour is anchored on the prompt shape that is actually graded

alternatives.option: Leave the decode alone and spend the time on more training
alternatives.reason: this is one 4-minute eval against a 40+ minute training round; if it is worth points it is worth them for free, and if it is not, the next card knows to spend the hours on data instead

alternatives.option: Tune temperature/top_p instead of going greedy
alternatives.reason: a temperature sweep is several evals for a parameter that has no reason to beat argmax on a single-sample-scored benchmark; greedy is the one setting that removes the variance entirely

alternatives.option: Self-consistency / majority voting
alternatives.reason: the grader scores one generation per item through inspect's generate(); there is no way to vote inside the model artifact

alternatives.option: Rejection-sampling fine-tuning (RFT) from exp-02 instead
alternatives.reason: the better card, but it is downstream of this one: RFT should be seeded from the strongest available checkpoint, and this run decides which that is. Planned as exp-05 with the ~1.7 h that remain after this.

alternatives.option: A third epoch on the same 60k rows
alternatives.reason: epoch 2 already repeats every row once; more unique problems is the cheaper source of signal than a third pass, and 3-epoch SFT on a 4B is where memorisation starts

alternatives.option: Add OpenMathInstruct-2's augmented_math (MATH-derived) rows for general math ability
alternatives.reason: the objective is GSM8K only; spending half the token budget on a harder, differently-formatted distribution trades measured in-domain data for speculative transfer

alternatives.option: All 124946 rows of sft_v2 at 1 epoch
alternatives.reason: one pass leaves the schedule short on optimizer steps (641 vs exp-02's 1034) on a corpus whose epoch-1 checkpoint was already the better one, and it gives up the second look at the human gsm8k rows entirely

alternatives.option: Keep the 2-epoch schedule now that epoch-1 is known to be the better exp-02 checkpoint
alternatives.reason: exp-02's own curve says 1034 steps on this recipe is past the optimum; 962 annealed steps is fewer steps AND a finished cosine, and it returns ~40 min to exp-05

alternatives.option: Scale the human gsm8k rows along with the OMI rows
alternatives.reason: there are only 7473 distinct human solutions, so scaling them means repeating them more; holding their absolute count fixed is what keeps this card a single-variable test of OMI volume

alternatives.option: Raise the learning rate to 2e-5 to get more out of the same steps
alternatives.reason: would confound the data change with an optimisation change; exp-02's 1e-5 run is the only calibrated point and this card is about data scale

alternatives.option: Rejection-sampling fine-tuning from the incumbent
alternatives.reason: the plan of record until exp-04 overran. Sampling k=4 over ~30k train problems plus a training pass plus an eval is ~1.6 h of the 3.65 h left, and it would leave no room for the larger-n read that actually decides which artifact ships. Weight averaging costs 17 s of CPU and one eval for a comparable expected gain.

alternatives.option: Ensemble / self-consistency over the two models at inference
alternatives.reason: the grader loads exactly one final_model directory and scores one generation per item; there is no place to put a second model

alternatives.option: Soup all four scored checkpoints
alternatives.reason: exp-04/s480 and exp-04/final are 480 and 1019 steps of one trajectory and exp-02/final is the weakest artifact at 0.6533; including them weights the exp-04 run 2:1 and drags in the checkpoint the greedy read already rejected. The two-model uniform average is the version whose weights need no justification.

alternatives.option: Weighted soup tuned on dev-150
alternatives.reason: with the two arms 0.7 pts apart on n=150 (floor 0.03) any mixing weight fitted to that set is fitting noise; uniform is the only choice not selected on the evaluation set

alternatives.option: Ship the n=150 winner and spend the remaining time on rejection-sampling fine-tuning
alternatives.reason: RFT needs ~1.6 h of the 3.5 h left and would have to be trained, packaged and scored before the deadline with no slack; picking the wrong artifact from a 0.7 pt gap is a live risk right now, and this read removes it for 45 min

alternatives.option: Re-score at --limit 500
alternatives.reason: the pre-declared tie-break from exp-04, but the full 1319-item set costs about twice as much for a 1.6x tighter interval and, unlike a 500-item prefix, is a superset of the dev-150 the earlier cards were selected on - so it cannot be gamed by the selection already made

alternatives.option: Repeat the n=150 evals with different seeds (C18)
alternatives.reason: greedy decoding is deterministic; repeating it returns the same numbers. The only way to shrink the interval is more items

alternatives.option: Also re-score exp-04/s480 and the exp-05 soup
alternatives.reason: both are further from the leader than the leader's own uncertainty and each costs another ~20 min; if the two-arm read finishes with time in hand, s480 can be added, but the card is decided on the two arms that can plausibly win

alternatives.option: Sample from BOTH checkpoints and pool the correct solutions, which was the design this card started from
alternatives.reason: measured throughput is 6.5k output tok/s, so one model over 11973 problems at k=4 takes ~53 min; two would take 1.8 h of the 3.1 h left and leave no margin to train, package and score before the deadline. Cut to the shipped model only, which is also the on-policy half - the half RFT actually depends on.

alternatives.option: Retrain from the base snapshot on sft_v3 plus the RFT rows
alternatives.reason: ~2 h, which does not fit; continuing from the shipped checkpoint keeps the 0.6399 behaviour as the starting point and only costs the ~15 min the RFT pass itself needs

alternatives.option: Keep only problems the model solves rarely (hard-example mining)
alternatives.reason: at k=4 the solve-rate estimate on a single problem is one of five values; selecting on it would filter mostly noise and would also strip the easy problems whose correct solutions are what stop the model drifting

alternatives.option: Stop here and ship the 0.6399 artifact
alternatives.reason: the genuinely safe option, and it stays available: final_model already holds that artifact, verified from disk, and this card only overwrites it if the pre-declared threshold is cleared. The cost of trying is time I would otherwise not use.

alternatives.reason: vLLM 10-shot decode at max-tokens 4000 costs roughly 3x the wall clock; 150 is the protocol default and every later card will reuse it

alternatives.option: Few-shot / decode-only fixes on the frozen parent (stop strings, lower temperature)
alternatives.reason: evaluate.py and templates/ are immutable and the parent snapshot is outside the working dir, so there is no decode knob I can set on the parent; and exp-01's first-ANSWER accuracy of 0.133 caps what termination alone could buy

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full fine-tuning
alternatives.reason: the parent has never seen the <start_of_turn>/<end_of_turn> frame at all; this is a format+behaviour shift over 153k rows, which is what full FT is for. Memory is not the constraint - 32768-token micro-batches fit

alternatives.option: MetaMathQA-395K as the corpus
alternatives.reason: its bodies carry gsm8k's own '#### N' line as well as a final 'The answer is: X', i.e. two answer markers, which is pitfall double_answer_format. OpenMathInstruct-2 has one boxed answer per solution and it is mechanically removable

alternatives.option: Start with a cheap 60k/1-epoch run for an early number
alternatives.reason: the pipeline is already validated end-to-end by the smoke runs below; checkpoints every 500 steps give the same early-stopping information inside one run

alternatives.option: Leave decode alone and spend the time on more training
alternatives.reason: this costs one 3-minute eval and no GPU training at all; every later card also inherits a variance floor of 3.3 pp under sampling versus ~0 under greedy, so it pays for itself in comparability alone

alternatives.option: Edit evaluate.py to pass temperature=0
alternatives.reason: forbidden by the task rules; the checkpoint's own generation_config.json is the only decode surface I own, and it is part of the model artifact the grader loads

alternatives.option: Self-consistency / majority vote over k samples
alternatives.reason: the grader reads exactly one completion per item (inspect match scorer on state.output.completion); there is nowhere to put a vote

alternatives.option: Score all four saved checkpoints (500, 1000, 1500, final)
alternatives.reason: each eval is ~4 min of GPU but ~7 min of protocol overhead; the epoch boundary is the one place the corpus says the sign can flip, and 500 (epoch 0.53) is clearly under-trained at loss 0.297 vs 0.22

alternatives.option: Skip this and go straight to a rejection-sampling round
alternatives.reason: the RFT round has to start from one checkpoint, and picking the wrong parent would carry the error into a 2 h experiment. 0.25 h now to fix the parent

alternatives.option: Compare at --limit 500 for a tighter interval
alternatives.reason: would break comparability with every card so far, which is the mistake pitfall comparator_protocol_mismatch names; n=150 greedy is at least deterministic now

alternatives.option: One annealed epoch over the SAME 153k rows
alternatives.reason: cheaper (1.25 h) and single-variable, but it would mostly reproduce the incumbent's weights with a better lr tail; the exp-04 diagnostic says the binding constraint is unseen target text, not schedule alone. This card takes both, at +0.75 h

alternatives.option: Score checkpoint-500 (epoch 0.53) first to find the accuracy peak
alternatives.reason: 0.3 h for information that would not change the action: whether the peak is at 0.5 or 1.0 epochs, the response is the same one annealed pass over a larger pool of distinct solutions

alternatives.option: Rejection-sampling round (sample k solutions from the incumbent, keep the correct ones, retrain)
alternatives.reason: scripts/rft_sample.py is written and ready, but it costs ~0.6 h of sampling before any training starts and it recycles the same ~80k problems the incumbent has already memorised once. Held as the next card if this one leaves time

alternatives.option: Add OpenMathInstruct-2's MATH-derived rows (augmented_math) for breadth
alternatives.reason: different domain and heavy LaTeX; it would change the output style the grader sees at the same time as the data volume, and there is no budget left to separate the two effects

alternatives.option: Keep the 2-solutions-per-problem cap and train on the 166714 rows that produces
alternatives.reason: the first build of pool_v2 showed train_2M is a DEEPER sample of the same augmented problems, not a wider one: 240101 rows were dropped by the cap and only ~11k new rows survived. Distinct problems are not available at this scale, so the axis had to change from 'more problems' to 'more solutions per problem', which is the axis OpenMathInstruct-2's own 1M/2M/5M/14M scaling plot is drawn along

alternatives.option: Just ship the incumbent on the n=150 numbers and spend the remaining time on a rejection-sampling round
alternatives.reason: an RFT round needs ~0.6 h of sampling plus ~0.8 h of training plus an eval, which does not fit in 3.4 h alongside packaging and verification; and it would be built on a parent chosen by a comparison the ruler cannot actually resolve

alternatives.option: Repeat both arms at n=150 with a different seed
alternatives.reason: the decode is greedy, so a repeat is bit-identical and buys nothing. The only way to shrink the interval here is more items

alternatives.option: Score the whole 1319-item test set
alternatives.reason: ~30 min per arm; at 3.4 h remaining that leaves no margin for packaging and the final load check, which is the one step whose failure costs everything (pitfall final_model_not_loadable)

alternatives.option: Also enter exp-05's checkpoint-1000/1500 as third and fourth arms
alternatives.reason: each extra arm is ~12 min and the card would stop being a single comparison; exp-05's whole trajectory is already known to sit below the incumbent at its own best point

alternatives.option: Ship exp-05's model on the n=500 result and stop
alternatives.reason: +2.4 pts at n=500 is 1.4 stderr, and exp-06 just demonstrated that a 2.7-point swing can come from read noise alone. The whole point of the last two cards was to stop deciding inside the noise

alternatives.option: Repeat the n=500 reads three times each and average
alternatives.reason: prices the read noise but not the sampling noise, and costs the same ~12 min as simply scoring every item once. Scoring all 1319 removes the sampling term entirely rather than estimating it

alternatives.option: Train something else with the remaining 3.1 h (rejection sampling, a third SFT recipe)
alternatives.reason: an RFT round is ~1.6 h before its first number and would leave no margin for packaging and the final load check. Choosing correctly between two models I already have is worth more than a third model I could not properly evaluate

alternatives.option: Keep using n=150 because every earlier card used it
alternatives.reason: comparability with earlier cards matters less than shipping the right checkpoint; both arms here are scored under the identical new protocol, so this card is internally consistent even though its n differs from exp-01..exp-05

alternatives.option: Trust that final_model/ is fine because it is a hard-link copy of ckpts/exp-05/final_greedy
alternatives.reason: the weights are certainly identical - the risk is not the tensors, it is evaluate.py's path-based template dispatch and vLLM loading a directory it has never been pointed at. That is exactly the class of failure the pitfall describes, and it costs the entire run

alternatives.option: The offline transformers load check in scripts/verify_final.py is enough
alternatives.reason: it already passed on this directory (loads, renders through templates/gemma3.jinja, terminates on <end_of_turn>, one ANSWER line, parses under match_str). But it uses transformers, not the grader's vLLM server, and it bypasses evaluate.py's argument handling entirely

alternatives.option: Re-run at --limit 150 to save four minutes
alternatives.reason: n=150 is the ruler this session has now measured to carry ~2.7 pp of read noise; a 150-item confirmation could differ from 0.7938 for reasons that have nothing to do with the artifact and would be unreadable

alternatives.option: Stop here and ship the verified 0.7976
alternatives.reason: that remains the outcome unless the soup wins on the identical full-test protocol; final_model/ is not touched until a number says to. The only thing at risk is 0.3 h

alternatives.option: A rejection-sampling round from the incumbent
alternatives.reason: ~1.6 h before its first number with 2.6 h left, and it would have to be packaged and re-verified afterwards. It is the right next experiment for a session with more clock, not this one

alternatives.option: Sweep the mixing weight (0.25/0.5/0.75)
alternatives.reason: each arm is ~5 min of merge plus ~4 min of eval and each is a separate card under the protocol; 0.5 is the uniform soup the literature reports and the one worth a single shot at this point in the clock

alternatives.option: Average in exp-02/final (the 2-epoch model) as a third ingredient
alternatives.reason: exp-04 measured it 4.7 points below its own epoch-1 checkpoint, so it is a known-worse ingredient and would need its own card to justify

alternatives.option: Stop and ship the verified 0.7976
alternatives.reason: still the outcome unless this run wins on the full-test protocol. final_model/ is not touched until a number says to, and the sampling that this card needed is already done and paid for

alternatives.option: Mix the RFT rows with a fresh slice of pool_v2 to guard against narrowing
alternatives.reason: those rows are exactly the ones the parent already consumed in exp-05, and exp-04 measured a second pass over already-seen targets at -4.7 points. Pure on-policy data keeps the single variable clean

alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and quote a published gemma-3-4b-pt GSM8K number
alternatives.reason: published numbers use a different prompt, fewshot count and answer extractor than inspect_evals/gsm8k with templates/gemma3.jinja; not a comparator under rule 2

alternatives.option: Measure the baseline at --limit 50 to save time
alternatives.reason: every later card will be scored at n=150; a comparator at a different --limit is not a comparator

alternatives.option: Fold the baseline into the first SFT card
alternatives.reason: the protocol requires a lock before any evaluation command, and the baseline number plus its failure taxonomy is itself the decision input for the first SFT card

alternatives.option: Few-shot prompt engineering / decode-config only, no training
alternatives.reason: the prompt and the number of shots are fixed by evaluate.py and inspect_evals/gsm8k; the only thing I control is the weights and the model directory's own configs

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full fine-tuning
alternatives.reason: the change needed is a behaviour change (terminate, follow a fixed output contract) across the whole distribution, which full FT does more reliably; memory is not the binding constraint once liger's fused CE removes the 262k-vocab logits tensor

alternatives.option: Train on the raw GSM8K train solutions (7473 rows)
alternatives.reason: too few rows for a base->instruct transformation, and their '<<3*4=12>>' calculator annotations are a second notation the grader never asked for

alternatives.option: MetaMathQA
alternatives.reason: its bodies carry gsm8k's own '#### N' line as well as a natural-language answer, i.e. two answer markers - pitfalls:double_answer_format. OpenMathInstruct-2 needs only \boxed flattening

alternatives.option: Train the full 77k-row corpus for 1 epoch
alternatives.reason: measured 6.1 samples/s => 3.5 h, more than a third of the remaining budget on an unvalidated first shot; 42k rows costs ~1.9 h and leaves room for a second card

alternatives.option: Pure-bf16 weights instead of fp32 master weights
alternatives.reason: benchmarked at 6.38 vs 6.09 samples/s - a 5% gain not worth bf16 rounding of 1e-5-scale AdamW updates

alternatives.option: Leave the sampled decode and buy the points with more training
alternatives.reason: training costs hours; this costs one eval and no weight change, and it compounds with every later card

alternatives.option: Pass decode flags on the command line
alternatives.reason: evaluate.py may not be modified (task rule 5) and the final grading run is launched by the harness, not by me - the model directory is the only channel I control

alternatives.option: Also sweep temperature 0.3/0.7 or min_p
alternatives.reason: single-sample accuracy on a math benchmark is maximised at greedy; a sweep costs 3 more evals for a decision already made by theory

alternatives.option: Continue training exp-02 on the unseen rows instead of restarting from base
alternatives.reason: cheaper (~1 h) but it stacks a second warm-up/cosine cycle on an already-converged checkpoint; a single clean schedule over 3.4x the unique data is the cleaner test of the data-quantity claim, and the budget affords it

alternatives.option: 2-3 epochs over the 42k rows exp-02 already used
alternatives.reason: unique problems beat repeats at this scale; the corpus has 159k pairs available and re-reading 42k of them cannot teach anything new

alternatives.option: Go straight to a rejection-sampling round from exp-03
alternatives.reason: RFT is the planned next card, but its yield depends on the parent's pass@k; running it from a stronger parent is strictly better, and the SFT is the thing that makes the parent stronger

alternatives.option: Add MATH / augmented_math rows for diversity
alternatives.reason: longer targets with latex the grader cannot read, for a grade-school benchmark; the \boxed-flattening filter already rejects most of them

alternatives.option: Raise --max-per-problem above 2 to get more rows
alternatives.reason: would buy near-duplicate solutions to problems already covered rather than new problems; 477739 rows were dropped by that cap and the pool is not the binding constraint

alternatives.option: Accept the WMA's defer and go straight to RFT (L3_worth_now=defer@0.55, L2_effect=[-0.01, 0.05])
alternatives.reason: I am launching anyway and recording the disagreement. The WMA's closest precedent (history r-2f4530d4/exp-08, +1.3 pp) scaled with MetaMathQA+ORCA-Math, a weaker corpus than verified-solution OpenMathInstruct-2, and on a different base. The published OpenMathInstruct-2 data-scaling ablation is the more relevant prior and it is not flat in the 40k-200k band. Countervailing fact the WMA is right about: gemma-3-4b-it reaches the high 80s on GSM8K, so 0.727 is far from a ceiling and the headroom is real. Cost 2.6 h of 8.0 h remaining still leaves the RFT round.

alternatives.option: Half-size arm (71k rows, ~1.3 h) first, as the WMA suggested
alternatives.reason: the 42k->71k delta would itself sit inside the 3 pp floor at n=150, so it would not decide anything, and the 1.3 h would then be spent again on the full arm

alternatives.option: Scale OpenMathInstruct-2 further (shards 11-31)
alternatives.reason: measured: 3 extra shards yielded 1243 new problems against 79240 already used. Further shards buy duplicate solutions to problems already covered, and exp-04 already showed 3.4x data is worth under 3 pts

alternatives.option: A second epoch over sft_v3
alternatives.reason: same off-policy distribution the model has converged on; the RFT rows are on-policy and verified, which is the strictly more informative signal at this point

alternatives.option: DPO or GRPO on correct/incorrect pairs
alternatives.reason: 4.3 h left. A preference or RL round needs a reward loop, a reference model in memory and hyperparameters I have no time to tune; a failed one costs the batch its remaining budget. RFT gets most of the on-policy benefit as plain SFT

alternatives.option: Train the RFT rows from the base snapshot on the union with sft_v3 (the canonical RFT recipe)
alternatives.reason: 200k+ rows from scratch is ~3.5 h and does not fit; continuing from exp-04 at a reduced lr with a 12000-row sft_v3 replay slice is the affordable variant

alternatives.option: RFT rows only, no replay
alternatives.reason: self-generated data at temperature 1.0 reinforces the model's own modes; a 17% replay slice of the verified off-policy corpus is cheap insurance against narrowing

alternatives.option: A second RFT round targeting the 5.9% of train problems unsolved at pass@4
alternatives.reason: sampling alone was 53 min last time and training another 70 min; it does not fit in 2.3 h with the packaging and verification still to do

alternatives.option: Soup exp-04/final with exp-05/final
alternatives.reason: those are a full RFT epoch apart and exp-04 is the measurably weaker of the two (0.768 vs 0.790 at n=500); averaging across that gap pulls toward the weaker parent rather than reducing noise around the better one

alternatives.option: Include checkpoint-540
alternatives.reason: at 25% of a cosine schedule the LR is still high and the weights are far from the tail; SWA works on the low-LR tail, and exp-04's step-2980 read (0.6933 vs 0.7533) is a direct measurement of how much a mid-trajectory point can cost

alternatives.option: Ship exp-05 and stop
alternatives.reason: that remains the fallback and final_model/ is not touched unless the soup wins under the identical protocol; this card costs one merge and one eval

alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and compare training runs against a published gemma-3-4b-pt GSM8K number
alternatives.reason: A literature number is not measured under this harness (10-shot inspect_evals/gsm8k, gemma3.jinja, vllm) and is not a legal comparator under rule 2.

alternatives.option: Fold the baseline into the first SFT card as an untracked side measurement
alternatives.reason: The eval is itself an evaluation experiment under CLAUDE.md and needs its own record; it also fixes the protocol (n, limit, max-connections) for every later card.

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of a full fine-tune
alternatives.reason: The intervention has to install turn termination and a new output format on a pretrained checkpoint - a large distribution shift, where LoRA is reported to trail full FT on math SFT. Memory is not the binding constraint: a token-budget batcher bounds the 262144-wide logit tensor and the smoke run fit.

alternatives.option: Few-shot prompt engineering / decode-config only
alternatives.reason: evaluate.py and templates/ are immutable, so the prompt is fixed; only the weights and the checkpoint's own generation_config are under my control.

alternatives.option: Train only on the 7473 native GSM8K train solutions
alternatives.reason: Native targets are terse 2-4 line derivations; OpenMathInstruct-2 gives ~9x more GSM8K-style problems with fuller reasoning. Native rows stay in the mixture at 1x so the harness's own 10-shot style remains in distribution.

alternatives.option: Include the MATH / augmented_math portion of OpenMathInstruct-2
alternatives.reason: Its targets are LaTeX-heavy and often non-integer, teaching a second answer surface the grader's last-number rule does not want; GSM8K answers are always integers.

alternatives.option: Two epochs over the existing 67472-row sft_v1 instead of one epoch over 141914 new-ish rows
alternatives.reason: Same GPU cost. The OpenMathInstruct-2 gsm8k pool holds ~134k rows at <=2 solutions per problem, so sft_v2 is mostly problems sft_v1 never saw; re-reading the same rows is the weaker use of the same hours.

alternatives.option: Go straight to a rejection-sampling round from exp-02
alternatives.reason: It is the right next lever but it is cheap (~1 h) and can be run from whichever SFT checkpoint wins; running it second means it starts from the stronger parent. Its sampling stage is being built during this card's lock wait so no time is lost.

alternatives.option: Add the augmented_math / MATH portion of OpenMathInstruct-2 to widen the mixture
alternatives.reason: Would change two things at once (volume and domain) and reintroduces the LaTeX/non-integer answer surface exp-02 deliberately excluded. Volume alone is the single variable being tested here.

alternatives.option: Raise the learning rate or train longer per row
alternatives.reason: exp-02's loss curve ended at 0.31 with grad_norm ~1.6 and no instability; nothing observed argues the optimisation was the limit, so the recipe is held fixed and only the data volume moves.

alternatives.option: Another SFT scale-up on the OpenMathInstruct-2 train_2M/train_5M splits
alternatives.reason: The gsm8k-derived pool of train_1M is already exhausted by sft_v2; a larger split means a download, a rebuild, a decontamination pass and another ~2.6 h of training, which does not fit in 4.5 h alongside anything else.

alternatives.option: A second full epoch over sft_v2 from exp-03
alternatives.reason: ~2.6 h for a re-read of rows already seen, against ~0.5 h for on-policy data the model has never been trained on.

alternatives.option: DPO on correct-vs-incorrect self-samples
alternatives.reason: The pairs exist for free from the same sampling run, but a preference stage is new machinery under 4.5 h of remaining budget and the SFT-shaped RFT round is the lower-variance use of the same data.

alternatives.option: Running with no intermediate checkpoints (the first version of this card)
alternatives.reason: The mixture is only ~21818 rows, about 243 optimizer steps, so the script's default save cadence of 500 would never fire and a late-epoch over-sharpen would leave nothing to fall back to inside the run. --save-steps 60 keeps four points on the trajectory for the cost of disk only.

alternatives.option: Rejection samples only, without replay
alternatives.reason: 10818 rows of the model's own text at 1 epoch is a narrow diet after a 141871-row corpus; an equal slice of sft_v2 is mixed in to hold the distribution. This does make the card a two-part intervention (on-policy rows + replay) rather than a single knob, which is recorded here deliberately.

alternatives.option: Ship exp-04 on the n=150 point estimate and stop
alternatives.reason: A 1.3-point gap at n=150 is a coin flip; 2.9 h remain and a 500-item read on both candidates costs about 30 min and cuts the standard error roughly in half.

alternatives.option: Repeat the n=150 eval on byte-identical weights to price the noise instead
alternatives.reason: Same GPU cost as going to n=500 but it measures the noise rather than reducing it; a larger n both reduces the error and gives a number closer to the full test distribution.

alternatives.option: Another training round (a second RFT pass, or a soup that includes exp-02)
alternatives.reason: 2.9 h minus this card's ~50 min leaves no room for a training round plus its evaluation and the final packaging; exp-02 at 0.687 is far enough behind that including it in the average is more likely to drag than to help.

alternatives.option: Score all four exp-04 step checkpoints as well
alternatives.reason: Four extra 500-item reads do not fit. The three candidates here are the only ones that can actually be shipped.

alternatives.option: Stop and ship exp-04
alternatives.reason: 2.3 h remain; this round reuses a code path that has already run end to end once (sample, mix, train, evaluate) and is guarded - final_model only changes if the candidate beats exp-04 at n=500.

alternatives.option: Download OpenMathInstruct-2 train_2M for ~134k genuinely new gsm8k-derived rows
alternatives.reason: Download, rebuild, decontamination and one epoch is ~2.4 h before any evaluation; it does not fit, and a truncated version of it would be a worse use of the same GPU minutes than a round that is known to complete in 21 min.

alternatives.option: Score exp-04's kept step checkpoints (60/120/180) instead
alternatives.reason: 196 steps on a cosine schedule to zero; the WMA's own L2 for checkpoint selection here is near zero and each read costs 3 min. The on-policy round has the larger upside.

alternatives.option: Raise the replay weight or drop replay entirely
alternatives.reason: The exp-04 recipe (roughly one replay row per on-policy row, lr 7e-6, one epoch) is the only version of this intervention with a measured outcome; changing two things at once in the last round would make the comparison unreadable.

alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and compare SFT runs to a published gemma-3-4b-pt GSM8K number
alternatives.reason: published numbers use a different prompt and scorer; protocol rule 2 requires the comparator measured under this exact protocol

alternatives.option: Baseline at --limit 50 to save ~10 minutes
alternatives.reason: every later card is compared to this; a smaller n would force a re-measure later

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of a full fine-tune
alternatives.reason: the change needed is behavioural (stop at <end_of_turn>, one answer line) plus a large math-CoT distribution shift; the full tune fits in 80 GB once the loss is masked, and a merged adapter is one more way final_model fails to load

alternatives.option: Train on openai/gsm8k train alone (7.5k rows)
alternatives.reason: 7.5k terse reference solutions is thin; OpenMathInstruct-2 gives 60k 405B-written solutions to GSM8K-train problems and their augmentations, and the native 7.5k are mixed in anyway at weight 2

alternatives.option: Prepend the grader's 10-shot prefix to every training row
alternatives.reason: it costs ~2050 extra prompt tokens on every row (about 2.5x the compute) for format reinforcement the target already carries; instead 10% of rows get a k-shot prefix, k in {2,4,6,8,10}, drawn from gsm8k TRAIN

alternatives.option: 3 epochs
alternatives.reason: at 16.85 samples/s that is 3.7 h of the 9.15 h left; 2 epochs is 2.5 h and the epoch-1 checkpoint is kept so both points can be read from one run

alternatives.option: Go straight to a rejection-sampling round and leave the decode alone
alternatives.reason: RFT is ~1.5 h of GPU; this is ~7 min on weights that already exist, and every later card would otherwise be measured under a decode I had never checked

alternatives.option: Fold the greedy switch silently into the next training card
alternatives.reason: two arms under different decode are not a comparison; the WMA precondition on exp-02 asked explicitly for a separate card

alternatives.option: Also sweep temperature 0.3/0.7
alternatives.reason: each point is another 7 min and the grader gives one sample per item, so the only question that matters is argmax vs the shipped sampler

alternatives.option: A third epoch, or more OpenMathInstruct-2 shards, from the same parent
alternatives.reason: exp-03 measured that a second pass over that mix already loses 4 pp; volume of distilled data is not the lever here

alternatives.option: Start the rejection-sampling stage from the epoch-2 checkpoint (the sampler's own parent)
alternatives.reason: epoch-2 is 4 pp behind epoch-1 greedy; the samples are only slightly off-policy for epoch-1, and 4 pp of parent quality is worth more than exact on-policy-ness

alternatives.option: Keep the original lr 1e-5 for this second stage
alternatives.reason: the parent is already tuned; the epoch-1-beats-epoch-2 result is direct evidence that further large steps on this task overshoot, so lr is halved to 5e-6

alternatives.option: Mix a slice of sft_train.jsonl back in against style collapse
alternatives.reason: the RFT rows are 25454 distinct problems in the model's own phrasing and already carry the exact target format; adding 20k distillation rows would cost ~15 min and re-introduce the data the epoch-2 result just penalised

alternatives.option: Re-sample the RFT set with random instead of shortest selection and repeat exp-04
alternatives.reason: exp-04's 133 -> 120 token shortening makes that the right diagnosis, but it is ~0.6 h of sampling plus ~0.5 h of training for an effect whose corpus base rate is near zero, and it would still be a second pass on top of a parent that punishes second passes

alternatives.option: Ship the incumbent and stop
alternatives.reason: 5 h remain, final_model already holds 0.7467, so the downside of one more card is bounded at the GPU time; a fully annealed single pass has never been tried on this model

alternatives.option: Add OpenMathInstruct-2's MATH and augmented_math rows for diversity
alternatives.reason: their solutions are LaTeX-heavy with non-integer answers; the format discipline that got 150/150 clean stops is worth more here than reasoning breadth on a GSM8K-only benchmark

alternatives.option: Raise the few-shot mix-in above 10% to match the grader's 10-shot prompt more closely
alternatives.reason: it multiplies token cost per row by roughly 15x on the affected rows, and the incumbent already stops correctly on 150/150 items, so format alignment is not what is failing

alternatives.option: Soup exp-04's checkpoints in as well
alternatives.reason: exp-04's weights measured 0.6933, 5.3 pp below the incumbent, and its 133 -> 120 token shortening is a behaviour I do not want averaged in

alternatives.option: A weighted soup favouring epoch 1
alternatives.reason: with only two ingredients a weight is a free parameter I would be fitting on the same 150 items I am grading on; the uniform average is the one point that needs no tuning

alternatives.option: GRPO / online RL from the incumbent

alternatives.reason: On-policy data alone is a narrow intervention over 7473 problems the model already solves 91% of; the 62,658 unseen 405B-generated rows are the part of the corpus exp-02 never saw and are the cheaper source of new competence. Both are mixed rather than run as two cards because each card costs ~15 min of lock and review overhead against a 5 h budget.

alternatives.option: DPO or GRPO on the 680 unsolved train problems
alternatives.reason: No preference pairs exist, a GRPO loop needs a reward server and several hours to tune, and the failure mode is capability rather than preference.

alternatives.option: Second epoch over sft_v1
alternatives.reason: 62,658 unseen rows of the same distribution are strictly better than a repeat of rows already fitted to loss 0.28.

alternatives.option: A third training stage
alternatives.reason: 3.4 h remain, the last training took 1.56 h and its reference class has a median effect of about zero; a soup costs 5 minutes of CPU and one eval.

alternatives.option: Weighted soup or a sweep over mixing coefficients
alternatives.reason: Each coefficient costs another eval at a ~3 pt noise floor, so a sweep at n=150 cannot resolve the differences it would produce. Uniform is the single pre-registered point.

alternatives.option: Adopt exp-04 anyway because it saw more data
alternatives.reason: The adoption rule was fixed in writing before exp-04 launched - beat 0.6867 by more than the noise floor or final_model does not move.

alternatives.option: Souping exp-04/checkpoint-900 in as a third ingredient
alternatives.reason: It is an unscored checkpoint from the middle of a cosine schedule; adding an unmeasured ingredient to the average makes a bad result uninterpretable. It is scored separately in this card instead.

alternatives.option: Ship the dev-150 leader without a wider read
alternatives.reason: The three gaps are 1 to 3 items out of 150 against a 5.7-item stderr; that is choosing on noise, and a wider read costs one eval per candidate.

alternatives.option: A fourth training stage or a coefficient sweep over soups
alternatives.reason: 3.15 h remain, training took 1.56 h last time for a null result, and every extra candidate needs its own n=1319 read to be rankable. Adding candidates makes the selection problem worse, not better.

alternatives.option: Repeat the n=150 read on each candidate instead (C18)
alternatives.reason: Greedy decoding is deterministic, so repeating the same 150 items returns the same number. Only new items add information, which is exactly what --limit -1 buys.

alternatives.option: Score the remaining unscored checkpoints (exp-04/checkpoint-900, -1800, exp-02/checkpoint-2000, -3000) as well
alternatives.reason: Each would need its own n=1319 read to be comparable, and the budget holds about three. Ranking the three already-scored candidates properly beats ranking seven of them badly.

alternatives.option: Stop here and ship the uniform soup
alternatives.reason: Still the default. This card cannot lose - final_model is only overwritten if the candidate wins the same n=1319 protocol - and 2.0 h of otherwise idle GPU pays for exactly one build and one read.

alternatives.option: Sweep several mixing coefficients
alternatives.reason: Each coefficient costs a 17-minute n=1319 read and the budget holds one. A single pre-registered point is the honest version; a sweep read at n=150 would be worthless given exp-06's finding that n=150 moves 1-3 items on identical weights.

alternatives.option: Add exp-04/checkpoint-900 or -1800 as a third ingredient
alternatives.reason: Both are unscored, so a bad result would be uninterpretable; and -1800 is 100 steps from final at an already-decayed learning rate, so it is nearly the same point.

alternatives.option: Another training stage
alternatives.reason: 2.0 h remain and the last one took 1.56 h; there is no room to train, package, evaluate and still leave the deliverable verified.

alternatives.option: Train on the original gsm8k train solutions (7.2k, terse '<<48/2=24>>' style)
alternatives.reason: 7.2k rows is ~10x too little to reshape a pretrained model's output contract, and OpenMathInstruct-2 already contains LLM-written solutions for those same train problems plus 140k augmentations of them

alternatives.option: Include augmented_math (algebra/geometry) rows in the mixture
alternatives.reason: GSM8K is grade-school arithmetic word problems; spending the first run's token budget off-domain is untested here. Held as a variable for a later card (build_data.py --n-math)

alternatives.option: Include the 10-shot eval system prefix on every row (exact prompt match)
alternatives.reason: the prefix is 2183 tokens vs a 139-token zero-shot prompt, so it would multiply the token budget by ~6; instead 5% of rows carry the exact 10-shot prefix and 15% carry 1-4 randomly drawn demos, which covers prefix-robustness at ~1.5x cost

alternatives.option: Skip this and spend the GPU hour on more training instead
alternatives.reason: one 6-minute eval decides what generation_config.json final_model/ ships; the historical corpus records a 0.087 -> 0.287 swing on identical weights from this single field, which is larger than anything a second training round is likely to buy

alternatives.option: Decide it on data/probe200.jsonl (my held-out train-split probe) instead of the benchmark protocol
alternatives.reason: the decision is about what ships, and the shipped config is read by the grader's vLLM; a probe measured through a different vLLM entry point (offline LLM API, generation_config='vllm') would not be the same protocol

alternatives.option: Also add repetition_penalty or a min_p floor
alternatives.reason: two changes in one card; temperature is the field with the evidence behind it, and 2 of 150 completions still hit the token cap, which greedy may either fix or worsen - that is what the diagnostic measures

alternatives.option: Rejection-sampling fine-tuning (sample k solutions from exp-02, keep the correct ones, retrain)
alternatives.reason: generation for even 15k problems x 4 samples is ~50 min of GPU before any training starts, and RFT re-trains on problems the model already fits (train loss 0.20). Cheaper first to spend the same GPU hours on 3.5x more distinct human-unseen targets; RFT stays available if this run leaves time

alternatives.option: Continue training exp-02/final on the new rows instead of restarting from base
alternatives.reason: sft_big.jsonl contains the same 80k problems exp-02 already fit twice, so continuing would be a third and fourth pass over them under a restarted schedule; from base every problem is seen ~3 times but with three DIFFERENT solutions, which is the variable being tested

alternatives.option: More epochs on the exp-02 mixture
alternatives.reason: exp-02's train loss was already 0.20 at the end of epoch 2 and its checkpoint-424 was lost, so there is no evidence a third pass over identical targets helps; distinct targets are the better use of the same tokens

alternatives.option: microsoft/orca-math-word-problems-200k as the extra data
alternatives.reason: it has no gold-answer field - the answer has to be guessed as the last number of a free-text solution, which is exactly the noise the grader is sensitive to. OpenMathInstruct-2 ships expected_answer for every row

alternatives.option: Train on all 279714 rows of sft_big.jsonl
alternatives.reason: measured 14.1k tokens/s => 2.9 h, against 6.4 h remaining that leaves no room for the eval, the final packaging and a fallback. 230k rows is 2.4 h

alternatives.option: Rejection-sampling fine-tuning from exp-04
alternatives.reason: with 3.5 h left it needs ~50 min of generation plus ~50 min of training plus an eval before anything can be shipped, and it would leave no margin to package and verify final_model/. The soup costs 5 minutes of CPU and is already measured on probe200

alternatives.option: The 3-way soup exp-02/final + exp-04/final + exp-04/checkpoint-820
alternatives.reason: measured on probe200 first: 0.8500, worse than the 2-way's 0.8750. Two checkpoints from the same trajectory pull the average toward that trajectory and cost the diversity the soup is for

alternatives.option: Ship exp-04_greedy and stop
alternatives.reason: leaves a candidate on the table that is 2.5 pts better on the only held-out set that is not the benchmark, for the price of one 7-minute eval

alternatives.option: Pick the soup on the strength of the probe200 number alone
alternatives.reason: probe200 items come from the gsm8k TRAIN distribution; the decision about what ships has to be confirmed under the grader's own protocol, which is what this card does

alternatives.option: Ship exp-04_greedy now on the strength of its n=150 number and spend the remaining time on another training round
alternatives.reason: no training round that starts with 3.1 h left can be trained, evaluated and packaged safely, and the selection error it would be layered on top of is ~3.4 pts - larger than anything exp-04 bought over exp-02

alternatives.option: Score at --limit 1319 (the whole test split)
alternatives.reason: n=150 took ~6 min, so 1319 items is ~50 min per candidate and 1.7 h for two, which does not leave enough margin to package and verify final_model/. n=500 cuts the standard error from ~0.034 to ~0.018 for ~20 min per candidate

alternatives.option: Break the tie on probe200 with more probe items
alternatives.reason: probe200 and the benchmark disagree by more than either standard error, and the probe is drawn from the gsm8k TRAIN distribution that both candidates were trained on augmentations of; adding probe items would sharpen the wrong measurement

alternatives.option: Also re-score exp-02_greedy at n=500
alternatives.reason: it is last or joint-last on both existing measurements (0.780 protocol, 0.835 probe200) and a third eval costs 20 min of a 3.1 h budget

alternatives.option: A rejection-sampling fine-tuning round with the remaining 2.7 h
alternatives.reason: generation + training + eval is ~1.75 h, leaving under an hour of margin, and exp-06 measured the paired sd of this protocol at 0.015 - an RFT gain of the size RFT plausibly delivers could not be distinguished from noise, so it would be shipped on a coin flip. exp-05 already made that mistake once

alternatives.option: Trust the byte-hash equality between final_model/ and ckpts/exp-04_greedy and skip the eval
alternatives.reason: the hash covers the safetensors shards; it does not cover config.json, generation_config.json, the tokenizer files or vLLM's ability to load the directory under a different name. evaluate.py also routes the chat template off the model PATH string first (model_type() greps for 'gemma' before falling back to config.json), and 'final_model' contains no such substring - that fallback has never been exercised in this session

alternatives.option: Verify at --limit 150 (7 min) rather than the full split
alternatives.reason: the full split costs ~50 min of a 2.7 h budget and buys the session's only low-variance number: stderr falls from 0.034 at n=150 to ~0.011 at n=1319

alternatives.option: Keep --max-connections 32 as first locked (WMA tier-2 precondition)
alternatives.reason: WMA cites a precedent where identical weights scored 0.2733 vs 0.8533 depending on request concurrency; a garbled comparator would poison every later card, so I re-locked at 8

alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and quote a published gemma-3-4b-pt GSM8K number
alternatives.reason: published numbers use a different prompt, template and decoding; not a comparator under this protocol

alternatives.option: Baseline at --limit 150 (the harness default)
alternatives.reason: stderr ~4pts is too coarse to rank arms; n=300 halves it and still contains the first 150 items the final grader uses

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full fine-tuning
alternatives.reason: the checkpoint has to learn a turn format and a stop token from scratch, a large behavioural change; the H100 fits full FT of 3.88B trainable params at ~40GB with an 8-bit optimiser, so there is no reason to constrain the update

alternatives.option: Train on openai/gsm8k train targets verbatim (7.5k rows, '#### N' style)
alternatives.reason: 7.5k rows is thin and those targets carry a second answer marker ('#### N' plus <<..>> calculator annotations), which is exactly the double_answer_format pitfall; OpenMathInstruct-2 already contains verified solutions for the same train problems plus ~230k augmented ones

alternatives.option: Add MATH / augmented_math rows for generality
alternatives.reason: GSM8K gold answers are always integers and the style is grade-school prose; the MATH subsets are LaTeX-heavy and would pull the output distribution away from the target. Held back as an exp-03 variable.

alternatives.option: Put the grader's 10-shot system prefix on every row
alternatives.reason: the prefix is 2228 tokens against a 184-token bare prompt, so it would quadruple the token bill for the same number of supervised tokens; 10% of rows carry it as insurance against a train/eval prompt mismatch

alternatives.option: Launch the locked data-volume run anyway (108k rows, 2 epochs, 3.2 h)
alternatives.reason: expected delta [-0.01, +0.04] against a +/-0.03 measurement floor, for 45% of the remaining budget; and its stated mechanism was wrong. Deferred behind the two cheaper cards (this one, then RFT), and only run if budget remains.

alternatives.option: Score exp-02/final at --limit -1 (n=1319) first so the comparator has a resolvable standard error
alternatives.reason: the WMA's tier-3 precondition #2, and correct in principle, but exp-02/final's 300 items took ~13 min at --max-connections 8, so n=1319 is ~55 min. That is affordable once, at the end, on the single candidate I actually submit - not now, on a comparator that is about to be replaced.

alternatives.option: Skip straight to RFT
alternatives.reason: checkpoint selection is 15 min and decides which checkpoint the RFT card samples from and starts from; doing it after RFT would mean sampling from a possibly worse parent

alternatives.option: The data-volume scale-up deferred from exp-03 (108k rows, 2 epochs, 3.2 h)
alternatives.reason: still priced at [-0.01,+0.04] by three same-type corpus precedents, and it would consume half the remaining budget. It stays deferred behind this cheaper card.

alternatives.option: Train from the base on sft_v1 + rft_v1 together (the classic RFT recipe), 2 epochs
alternatives.reason: 2.6 h rather than 0.6 h, and it changes two things at once (parent and mixture) so a null result would not say which. If this card lands, that is the shape of the follow-up run

alternatives.option: Mix a slice of sft_v1 into the RFT continuation to guard against distribution narrowing
alternatives.reason: it is the safer engineering choice but it confounds 'on-policy data' with 'more offline data'; instead the run is kept short (1 epoch) at a halved lr (5e-6), and the format diagnostic plus the paired read against exp-02 will show narrowing if it happens

alternatives.option: Sample at temperature 0.7 instead of 1.0
alternatives.reason: lower temperature raises the per-sample hit rate but collapses the diversity of derivations, which is the thing rejection sampling is supposed to harvest; k=4 at t=1.0 with de-duplication on the first 120 characters keeps distinct chains

alternatives.option: 2 epochs over the same 150k rows (4.1 h)
alternatives.reason: would not fit the remaining budget with an evaluation and a packaging step after it, and exp-03 measured that a second epoch over this recipe's data is worth ~0 (0.730 vs 0.710, p=0.50). One epoch over 2.9x the rows spends the same tokens on new material instead.

alternatives.option: Continue from exp-02/final or exp-04/final instead of the base checkpoint
alternatives.reason: the parent has already seen 51k of these 108k rows twice; continuing would make the run a third and fourth pass over that subset. Starting from base gives every row the same single exposure and makes the comparison against exp-02 a clean data-quantity contrast at ~1.35x the token bill

alternatives.option: Add the 60k orca-math rows built earlier (data/sft_v2.jsonl)
alternatives.reason: rejected in exp-03 on measurement: 2 of 3 spot-checked rows had a wrong extracted answer because orca-math ships no gold answer field

alternatives.option: Spend the same 2 h taking exp-02/final to --limit -1 (n=1319) instead of training
alternatives.reason: the WMA's tier-4 suggestion and worth doing, but it measures a candidate rather than producing a better one; it is scheduled after this run, on whichever checkpoint leads at n=300, if the budget holds

alternatives.option: A second epoch over sft_v4 continuing from exp-05/final (~1 h for half an epoch, then eval)
alternatives.reason: exp-03 measured a second epoch over this recipe's data at 0.730 vs 0.710 with McNemar p=0.50, i.e. nothing, and a partial second epoch under a cosine schedule already annealed to zero is worse than that. It would also finish with under 40 min of slack against a submission that is already in place and verified.

alternatives.option: Weight-average exp-05/final with exp-02/final (model soup)
alternatives.reason: souping helps when the ingredients are of similar quality; exp-02 is 6 pts worse on the same 300 items, so the expected result is a model between the two, with no time left to measure it properly afterwards

alternatives.option: Score exp-05's checkpoint-3400 as well (C5 lever)
alternatives.reason: checkpoint-3400 is 98.4% of the way through a one-epoch cosine schedule, so it differs from final/ by 54 steps at a learning rate near zero; the C5 lever needs checkpoints that are actually apart, which --save-steps 1700 did not produce

alternatives.option: Stop now and leave 2.1 h unused
alternatives.reason: the submission's only measurements are a 300-item and a 150-item read; a full-test read costs ~55 min, cannot damage the artifact, and is the difference between reporting 0.77 +/- 0.024 and reporting a number with a ~1.2 pt interval

alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and train first
alternatives.reason: every later card needs a comparator measured under the same protocol; without it deltas are unreadable

alternatives.option: Baseline at --limit 500 for tighter CI
alternatives.reason: evaluate.py documents 150 as the good limit; a 500-item baseline could not be compared to cheap 150-item iteration evals

alternatives.option: --max-connections 16 for speed (the original locked argv)
alternatives.reason: WMA verdict exp-01.verdict.json e7: corpus has 0.2733 vs 0.8533 for concurrency 8 vs 2 on byte-identical greedy weights (99/150 completions began '!!!!'), plus EngineDeadError at 8/16. This number is the ruler for the whole session, so it is bought at the default concurrency 2.

alternatives.option: Strip do_sample/top_k/top_p from the base snapshot so the baseline is greedy
alternatives.reason: the snapshot is immutable for this batch; the base floor must be the artifact as shipped. Greedy decoding is instead an explicit part of the candidate artifact (its own generation_config.json) and is measured as such.

alternatives.option: Fix termination by decode configuration alone, no training
alternatives.reason: evaluate.py is immutable and sends no stop_seqs; 106 (<end_of_turn>) is already in the checkpoint's eos_token_id, so the model simply never emits it. Only the weights can change that.

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full fine-tuning
alternatives.reason: the change needed is a base->instruct format transformation at every token position, not a narrow skill graft; an H100 fits full fp32-master training of 4B with 8-bit Adam, so the cheaper method buys nothing here

alternatives.option: Train on GSM8K train alone (7173 rows)
alternatives.reason: 7k terse human solutions is thin for teaching a reasoning style and a turn discipline at once; public GSM8K-train-derived augmentations add ~50k rows at no contamination cost (checker: 0/56785 flagged)

alternatives.option: Mix in MATH-derived rows for transfer
alternatives.reason: the benchmark is grade-school word problems and the budget allows roughly two training runs; spend all of it in-domain

alternatives.option: per-device batch 16 (the first locked value)
alternatives.reason: WMA e2: the binding term is the loss path, not the weights - 16 x 1024 x 262144 logits upcast to fp32 is ~43 GB of transient peak on top of ~48 GB resident. An 8-step smoke at bs 16 did survive, but group_by_length feeds the longest megabatch first over the FULL file and the smoke saw only a 2000-row slice, so the batch that would OOM had not been drawn yet. bs 8 x grad_accum 4 holds the effective batch at 32 and halves that peak.

alternatives.option: drop the fp32 master weights instead of the batch size, to buy the same memory
alternatives.reason: that is the one saving that costs accuracy: at lr 1e-5 the update/weight ratio is ~1e-3 and bf16's relative eps is ~4e-3, so a large share of updates would round to nothing. Pay for it in batch size instead.

alternatives.option: Train with the harness's 10-shot system message in the prompt
alternatives.reason: it would add ~1700 prompt tokens to every row (6x the token budget) for a prefix the model sees only at grading time; instead the 0-shot-trained model is probed on the watch set WITH that prefix, so the mismatch is measured rather than assumed

alternatives.option: Ship exp-02/best as the final model and spend the remaining time on RFT instead
alternatives.reason: RFT attacks wrong_answer (65 items). The prefix effect is a separate 20-item bucket that no amount of extra correct-chain data addresses, and it is measured, not hypothesised. Do the measured one first; RFT is exp-04 if time allows.

alternatives.option: Retrain from base with few-shot prefixes mixed in from the start
alternatives.reason: ~3 h for a full re-run against ~40 min for a continuation, with 6.6 h left and no candidate yet evaluated on the harness

alternatives.option: Continue from checkpoint-3546 (the end of training) instead of 1800
alternatives.reason: 3546 is the damaged checkpoint: 80/300 non-terminating under the prefix. 1800 (one epoch) is both the dev-best and the one whose termination is intact

alternatives.option: Train only on 10-shot-prefixed rows
alternatives.reason: the model must stay good 0-shot too - that is where its 0.740 lives - and an all-prefix diet risks teaching it to expect exemplars. The mix keeps 3/8 of rows at 0 shots.

alternatives.option: keep per-device batch 8

alternatives.option: Score every one of exp-04's 8 checkpoints
alternatives.reason: taking the max of 8 noisy reads inflates the winner by more than the extra coverage is worth. Four candidates - the three the clean-dev sweep ranked highest, plus the previous card's model - keeps the selection bias near one standard error

alternatives.option: Score on the full 1319-item test set

alternatives.option: Keep exp-04/checkpoint-250 because the grader's default is --limit 150

alternatives.option: Bootstrap the existing 500-item logs instead of running more items
alternatives.reason: resampling cannot create information the 500 items do not contain; the disagreement is about the 819 items nobody has scored
