alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and start training immediately
alternatives.reason: every later card needs a comparator measured under the same protocol; without it no delta is interpretable

alternatives.option: Baseline at --limit 500 for tighter error bars
alternatives.reason: the harness default and the protocol for this batch is --limit 150; a comparator must use the same n

alternatives.option: Score the base snapshot as shipped (sampled decode)
alternatives.reason: WMA precondition tier-1 accepted. evaluate.py passes no temperature, so vLLM takes the decode from generation_config.json; the shipped file has top_k 64 / top_p 0.95 / no temperature, i.e. temperature 1.0 sampling, while any Trainer-saved candidate would decode greedily - every later delta would silently mix a decode change with the training. The batch protocol is therefore frozen as GREEDY for base and candidates alike: models/gemma3_base_greedy symlinks the immutable snapshot's weights and overrides only generation_config.json (temperature 0.0). Base weights are untouched.

alternatives.option: --max-connections 2 (the script default, WMA-preferred)
alternatives.reason: tried first and abandoned. The base at greedy never emits <end_of_turn>: all 20 completions of the conn=2 n=20 smoke ran to the 4000-token cap, and the n=150 conn=2 run was managing 24 samples in 11 min (~70 min projected) for a number already known to be ~0. The batch protocol is therefore conn=16, with analyze_log.py's garbage counter (repeated-punctuation prefix) as the mechanical guard against the concurrency corruption the WMA warned about; the first trained candidate will additionally be scored at conn=2 and conn=16 to show the two agree.

alternatives.option: A repeat read of the same 150 to measure the sampling spread (WMA cheaper_variant tier-4)
alternatives.reason: not needed once the protocol is greedy: decode is deterministic, so the repeat would only measure vLLM batching jitter

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full-parameter SFT
alternatives.reason: the model has to learn a behaviour it does not have at all (stop at <end_of_turn>, answer in a fixed shape) and there is GPU headroom for a full 3.9B update at 9.6k tok/s; LoRA would only be needed if memory forced it

alternatives.option: Train only on the 7.1k original gsm8k train chains
alternatives.reason: their chains are terse and calculator-annotated; the measured smoke throughput allows ~31M tokens/epoch, so 69k rows of longer natural-language chains fit in the same hour and give ~10x the supervision

alternatives.option: MetaMathQA-395K instead of OpenMathInstruct-2
alternatives.reason: MetaMathQA targets carry 'The answer is: n' as a second answer marker (the double_answer_format pitfall) and its chains are older-model rephrasings; OpenMathInstruct-2's gsm8k subsets are 405B-generated chains and were reformatted here to a single ANSWER: marker

alternatives.option: Include the exact 10-shot eval prefix on every training row
alternatives.reason: would cost ~2200 prompt tokens per row (7x the corpus). 15% of rows instead carry a random 1-10 shot prefix drawn from gsm8k train, which teaches robustness to a prefix without paying for it on every row

alternatives.option: 1 epoch
alternatives.reason: cheaper by 55 min but an SFT this size normally still improves on the second pass; a checkpoint is saved at each epoch so both are scored and the cheaper one can still win

alternatives.option: Retrain from the base on sft_v1 + rft_v1 for 2 epochs (the canonical RFT recipe)
alternatives.reason: 46M tokens/epoch = ~2.6 h of the 6.9 h left, leaving no room to score it or to recover if it lost to the incumbent; continuing from exp-02 for one epoch costs ~30 min

alternatives.option: A third SFT epoch on sft_v1
alternatives.reason: epoch 1 -> epoch 2 moved dev-250 only 0.716 -> 0.736 while train loss fell to 0.31; more passes over the same chains is the flattest lever available

alternatives.option: DPO on correct-vs-incorrect sampled pairs
alternatives.reason: the 14% of questions never solved at k=4 give few clean pairs, and a preference run needs a reference model in memory plus a tuning pass this batch has no budget to debug

alternatives.option: RFT rows only, no replay
alternatives.reason: self-generated chains are a narrower style than the 405B-written ones exp-02 learned; 15k rows resampled from sft_v1 are mixed in (37% of the file) to hold the distribution

alternatives.option: Keep all correct samples per question
alternatives.reason: mean 2.55 correct of 4 would over-weight easy questions; capped at 2 per question after de-duplicating near-identical chains

alternatives.option: A second RFT round from exp-03 with k=8 on the questions it fails
alternatives.reason: the first round returned ~1 pt from chains the model could already produce; a second round starts from a smaller pool of unsolved questions and should return less

alternatives.option: Uniform soup of exp-02/final and exp-03/final
alternatives.reason: cheap (~15 min) and kept in reserve as exp-05, but a soup of two checkpoints 1 pt apart is a variance-reduction move worth ~0.5 pt, not the 2.5 h of GPU still available

alternatives.option: Continue exp-03 on the larger corpus instead of restarting from the base
alternatives.reason: exp-03 has already had two annealed cosine schedules; a third restart on largely-overlapping data is where the flat returns of exp-03 came from. Training the enlarged corpus from the immutable base is the clean comparison and reuses the recipe that produced the +70 pt step

alternatives.option: 2 full epochs on the 111k corpus
alternatives.reason: 57.4M tokens/epoch at the measured 9.6k tokens/s is 100 min/epoch, so 2 epochs = 3.3 h of the 5.95 h left and would leave no room to score, package and verify. 1.5 epochs anneals the cosine properly and saves a fallback checkpoint at epoch 1

alternatives.option: Download more OpenMathInstruct-2 shards
alternatives.reason: not needed: the 4 shards on disk hold far more unique augmented_gsm8k problems than the 52k this build takes, and download time would come out of training time

alternatives.option: A third training run (more data, or 2 full epochs on sft_v2)
alternatives.reason: an epoch of sft_v2 costs 1.6 h of the 3.5 h left and would leave no margin for scoring, packaging and the final_model load check - the pitfall the preflight names as the one that voids a whole batch

alternatives.option: Soup exp-04/final with exp-03/final or exp-02/final
alternatives.reason: exp-03 and exp-02 descend from a different run than exp-04 (exp-04 restarts from the base), so their weights are not in a shared basin; averaging across runs of a 4B model usually destroys it, and there is no budget to recover from that

alternatives.option: Submit exp-04/final now and stop
alternatives.reason: that is exactly the fallback if this card fails; the soup costs ~6 min of CPU plus one 3 min read, and the incumbent is untouched on disk either way

alternatives.option: A weighted soup or a 3-point soup including checkpoint-660 of exp-02
alternatives.reason: a weight ratio is another free parameter that a 0.013-floor read cannot fit, and checkpoint-660 belongs to a different run

alternatives.option: A second rejection-sampling round from exp-04
alternatives.reason: ~20 min of sampling before any training, and exp-03 measured what a round of the model's own chains is worth here: +1.1 pts, z = 1.04. Fresh 405B-written chains on unseen problems cost no sampling time and are the ingredient exp-04 showed pays

alternatives.option: Retrain from the base on sft_v2 + sft_v3_fresh (168k rows)
alternatives.reason: 88M tokens/epoch = 2.5 h against 3.1 h left; there would be no margin to score it, repackage final_model and re-verify, and the current submission would be at risk

alternatives.option: Stop here and spend the remaining time on the record
alternatives.reason: final_model is already installed and verified end to end through the grader's own default invocation (0.7067 at n=150, 0 truncated); this card cannot damage it, because the incumbent stays on disk and is only replaced if the new checkpoint wins the paired full-test count

alternatives.option: Higher lr than 5e-6 for the continuation
alternatives.reason: exp-03's continuation at 5e-6 held its parent's behaviour and gained ~1 pt; a larger step on a checkpoint that has already annealed twice risks the regression pattern exp-03 showed on dev-250 (19 regressions for 15 fixes)

alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and compare against the published Gemma-3-4B-pt GSM8K number (38.4, 8-shot CoT)
alternatives.reason: different harness, prompt and decode config; rule 2 needs a comparator measured under this exact protocol

alternatives.option: Baseline on the full test set (--limit 1319)
alternatives.reason: ~9x the wall clock; --limit 150 is evaluate.py's stated default and will be the protocol for every card in this batch

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full-parameter SFT
alternatives.reason: a pt checkpoint has to learn a turn-terminating instruct behaviour it has never seen, which is a large distribution shift; the memory probe showed full FT peaks at 42 GiB of 80 GiB, so there is no reason to take the LoRA capacity hit

alternatives.option: Train on the original GSM8K train solutions (7473 terse chains)
alternatives.reason: 8x less data, weaker chains, and their '####' marker is a second answer marker the grader could read (pitfalls.yaml double_answer_format)

alternatives.option: MetaMathQA-395K
alternatives.reason: its bodies carry gsm8k's own '#### N' line as well as a boxed answer, which is exactly the double-marker failure; OpenMathInstruct-2 has one boxed marker per solution that unwraps cleanly

alternatives.option: Render every training row with the full 10-shot system message so training matches grading exactly
alternatives.reason: that prefix is 2044 tokens and identical on every row: it would quadruple the token bill for one fixed string. Instead 10% of rows carry a k-shot prefix, k in {2,4,6,8,10}, drawn from the very same 10 exemplars the grader uses.

alternatives.option: Leave decoding alone and spend the time on another training round
alternatives.reason: training rounds cost hours and this costs one 4-minute eval; and until the decode config is settled every later comparison carries the ~3.9 pp sampling noise this eval's stderr reports

alternatives.option: Self-consistency / majority vote over k samples
alternatives.reason: the harness scores one completion per item; there is no place to put a vote

alternatives.option: Tune temperature on a grid (0.2/0.4/0.7)
alternatives.reason: for a model graded on a single sample, greedy dominates a positive temperature except when it degenerates into a loop; one eval tells me whether it degenerates, and a grid costs four

alternatives.option: Evaluate all four kept checkpoints
alternatives.reason: four evals for a curve when one contrast answers the question I actually have (is the second epoch helping or overfitting); the two intermediate points only matter if the answer is 'overfitting', and then 629 is the next read

alternatives.option: Skip this and start the rejection-sampling round from the epoch-2 weights
alternatives.reason: if epoch 2 overfit, every hour of the RFT round would be spent on the wrong parent; the check costs 5 minutes against a 2.5 h round

alternatives.option: Retrain from the base checkpoint on SFT+RFT combined (the canonical RFT recipe)
alternatives.reason: 2 epochs over ~146k rows is ~4 h and I have 5.8; continuing the incumbent for one epoch at a lower LR is the same intervention at a quarter of the price, and it keeps the 0.7267 checkpoint intact as a fallback

alternatives.option: A third epoch, or a second solution per problem from OpenMathInstruct-2
alternatives.reason: exp-04 measured that direction as flat; the data would still be off-policy 405B-generated chains the model has already been fitted to

alternatives.option: DPO on correct/incorrect sample pairs from the same generation run
alternatives.reason: the pairs exist for free, but preference training on a model whose errors are arithmetic slips rather than style is a weaker lever than simply training on more of its own correct arithmetic, and it needs a second card's worth of plumbing I cannot verify in the time left

alternatives.option: Keep all 4 correct chains per question
alternatives.reason: it would triple-count the easy questions the model already solves 4/4; capping at 2 and preferring the shortest correct chains keeps the frontier questions proportionally heavier

alternatives.option: Enlarge the corpus with unseen GSM8K-style problems from OpenMathInstruct-2's train_5M split
alternatives.reason: measured and dead: train_5M's gsm8k portion holds 80840 unique problems against the 80505 already used - 335 new ones. The larger splits add solutions per problem, not problems.

alternatives.option: Raise the share of training rows carrying the grader's 10-shot prefix above 10%
alternatives.reason: the probe puts that whole effect at 1.75 points on n=800, inside its own noise; it would cost ~30% more tokens per epoch to chase

alternatives.option: microsoft/orca-math-word-problems-200k as a new problem source
alternatives.reason: 200k genuinely new word problems, but no gold-answer field - the final answer would have to be heuristically read out of the solution prose, so nothing could be answer-verified, and the distribution is visibly off (Korean-translated puzzle phrasing) for a GSM8K target

alternatives.option: Ship the incumbent on the n=150 read and stop
alternatives.reason: it is the safe default and it is what happens if this card fails, but a 2-point n=150 gap is a coin flip: an 8x larger read costs 40 minutes of a 3.7 h remainder and turns the shipping decision from a guess into a measurement

alternatives.option: Repeat both n=150 reads a few times and average
alternatives.reason: greedy decoding is deterministic, so a repeat of the identical invocation returns the identical number; the only way to shrink this interval is more items

alternatives.option: Also score exp-05/checkpoint-570 and exp-02/checkpoint-1887
alternatives.reason: more arms at 20 minutes each would eat the margin I need to package and verify final_model; the two arms that matter are the two candidates

alternatives.option: Stop here and ship the incumbent
alternatives.reason: that is the fallback and final_model already holds it; a soup costs one 4-minute eval and cannot damage the fallback, which stays on disk untouched

alternatives.option: Sweep the mixing weight (0.25/0.5/0.75)
alternatives.reason: three arms for a lever whose whole expected effect is 1-2 points; the parents are equal in score, so the uniform average is the only point on the line I can justify without a validation set separate from the thing I am measuring on

alternatives.option: Soup in exp-02/checkpoint-1258 and 1887 as well
alternatives.reason: 1258 measured 1.3 points behind, and the intermediate checkpoints are earlier points on the same trajectory rather than independent runs: they add correlation, not diversity

alternatives.option: Another training round with the time left
alternatives.reason: 3.3 h minus the packaging margin is one 1-hour round at best, and the last two data interventions - a second epoch, then rejection sampling - both landed inside the noise band. A merge is the one remaining lever that needs no new data.

alternatives.option: Ship without running the directory, since its weight files are hardlinks to already-scored inodes
alternatives.reason: the inodes are provably identical, but the thing that has never been exercised is evaluate.py's own path handling on this directory name: model_type() first greps the path string for 'gemma' and only then falls back to reading config.json. 'final_model' contains no 'gemma', so the fallback is what decides the template. Verified reasoning is not a verified run, and I have 3 h.

alternatives.option: Verify with a --limit 20 smoke instead of the full set
alternatives.reason: the full set costs 4 minutes here and gives the shipped artefact's actual headline number instead of a plumbing check; there is no reason to buy the cheaper one

alternatives.option: Spend the remaining 3 h on one more training round
alternatives.reason: three consecutive interventions have landed inside the noise floor, and an unverified final_model is a way to score 0 rather than 0.73. Verification first; there is no time left after it for a round that could beat the plateau.

alternatives.reason: it cannot teach the model to emit <end_of_turn>, which is the dominant failure. The greedy half of that lever is folded into this card's saved checkpoint and isolated by this card's diagnostic instead of costing a separate GPU hour

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full fine-tuning
alternatives.reason: the model has to learn a stop behaviour and a new answer format, not just a task skill; full FT of 3.9B text params fits in 80GB with grad checkpointing at batch 8 x accum 8, and it rules out adapter-merge failure at submission (pitfalls.yaml final_model_not_loadable)

alternatives.option: Train on the raw gsm8k train solutions alone (7,473 rows)
alternatives.reason: 7.5k terse targets is thin coverage; OpenMathInstruct-2's gsm8k / augmented_gsm8k splits add ~30k longer, more explicit chains over the same and adjacent problems

alternatives.option: Include OpenMathInstruct-2's augmented_math split (277k rows of MATH-derived problems)
alternatives.reason: its answers are symbolic LaTeX, not integers; the grader reads the last number-like token, so those targets teach a shape the grader cannot score

alternatives.option: Train with the 10-shot system message on every row
alternatives.reason: the 10-shot prefix is 2160 tokens against 116 for the bare prompt, so it would roughly triple the epoch cost; 10% of rows carry it as insurance against a train/grade context mismatch

alternatives.option: Scale the corpus only (84,725 rows, no on-policy data)
alternatives.reason: the rejection-sampled chains are already paid for - the sampling ran on the GPU while this card was being written - and on-policy correct chains are the one data source that is guaranteed to be reachable for this model

alternatives.option: Rejection-sampling data only, no corpus scaling
alternatives.reason: RFT rows concentrate on problems the incumbent can already solve at temperature 1; without fresh unique problems the run mostly re-teaches what exp-02 knows

alternatives.option: Continue training from ckpts/exp-02/final instead of restarting from the base snapshot
alternatives.reason: exp-02 already made two passes over 37k of these same rows; a third and fourth pass over them from a converged checkpoint is where over-fitting lives. Restarting from base is also what the RFT literature does, and it keeps exp-03 a clean single-parent card

alternatives.option: Raise the learning rate above 1e-5 or extend to 3 epochs
alternatives.reason: two changes at once (data and schedule) with no way to attribute the result; lr and epoch count stay exactly at exp-02's values so the delta is the data

alternatives.option: Add OpenMathInstruct-2 train_2M/train_5M shards for more unique problems
alternatives.reason: train_1M already yields 63,437 unique augmented_gsm8k problems, more than two epochs can consume in the remaining budget; the download would cost ~20 min of wall clock for rows that would never be read

alternatives.option: A third training run (second RFT round from exp-03, or a 3-epoch schedule)
alternatives.reason: exp-03's two epochs took 3.27 h; even a one-epoch run on the same corpus is ~1.6 h plus sampling, which does not fit in 2.6 h with the finalisation and verification still to do

alternatives.option: Average exp-03/final with exp-03/checkpoint-1500 instead
alternatives.reason: those two are 314 steps apart at a cosine LR already below 1e-7, so they sit almost on top of each other in weight space; averaging them cannot move much. exp-02 and exp-03 are two full independent fine-tunes from the same init, which is the case where weight averaging actually behaves like an ensemble

alternatives.option: Spend the remaining time on a --limit 1319 read of exp-03 instead of trying anything new
alternatives.reason: the exp-03 verdict recommended it, but the adopt decision is already carried by two independent reads moving together (dev-150 +3.3, held-out probe +2.3), and a full read cannot raise the score. A confirmation read is scheduled after this card only if the soup wins and time remains

alternatives.option: Adopt the soup on the 300-item probe alone to save one eval
alternatives.reason: the probe is held-out gsm8k TRAIN, not the benchmark; every adopt decision in this batch has been made on the protocol read and this one will be too

alternatives.option: Ship without a full-n read
alternatives.reason: the whole submission rests on a 150-item number and on the assumption that final_model/ is a working copy of ckpts/exp-03/final; both are cheap to check and neither has been checked end to end

alternatives.option: Another training or merge attempt in the remaining 2 h
alternatives.reason: exp-03's run took 3.27 h and exp-04 showed the cheap merge lever does not pay here; anything that would fit cannot be validated before the deadline

alternatives.option: Read at --limit 500 instead of the full test set
alternatives.reason: the full set costs roughly 15 min at the measured 1.5 min per 150 items and removes sampling error from the headline number entirely; there is no reason to prefer a partial read at this point

alternatives.option: Use --limit 1319 (full test) for the baseline
alternatives.reason: 9x the GPU time for a number only used as a comparator; --limit 150 is the harness default and is what every later card will use

alternatives.option: Characterise failures by hand-reading the base model's outputs without running the official script
alternatives.reason: would not exercise templates/gemma3.jinja, which is the very thing pitfall template_unreachable says to verify

alternatives.option: Keep --max-connections 32 for speed and count garbage-prefixed outputs afterwards

alternatives.option: Force greedy decoding for the baseline by editing a copy of the base generation_config.json
alternatives.reason: the base weights must not drift and the comparator must be the model as shipped; the decode question is worth its own card (planned exp-03) measured against this one

alternatives.option: Also run --limit 1319 now for a tighter estimate
alternatives.reason: the WMA notes n=50 vs n=150 have differed by 26-29 pp in this corpus, so the protocol must be pinned at one n; 150 is the harness default and every later card will reuse it

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full-parameter SFT
alternatives.reason: the H100 fits a full 3.88B fine-tune at 55 GB with the chunked-CE loss, and full FT removes the adapter-merge step and the final_model_not_loadable pitfall with it

alternatives.option: Train on GSM8K train alone (7,473 rows)
alternatives.reason: too small to move a 4B base model far; OpenMathInstruct-2 supplies 80k verified-answer augmentations of the same distribution at no extra cost

alternatives.option: Reproduce the grader's full 10-shot system message in every training prompt
alternatives.reason: 2,044 extra prompt tokens per row is ~5x the compute for a prompt-side match; instead 10% of rows carry a 1-4 shot prefix in the grader's exact exemplar format as a cheap robustness hedge

alternatives.option: Include much more augmented_math (MATH-style, symbolic)
alternatives.reason: GSM8K is grade-school arithmetic word problems; 10k rows are kept for robustness, more would spend the token budget off-distribution

alternatives.option: Set temperature 0 in the trained model's generation_config now
alternatives.reason: it would confound the SFT effect with a decode change; exp-01 established the comparator under the shipped sampling decode, so exp-02 keeps it and exp-03 tests decode alone

alternatives.option: Go straight to a rejection-sampling round and leave the decode alone
alternatives.reason: an RFT round costs ~1.5 h and would be measured against a noisy sampling read; the decode change costs 5 minutes of GPU and, per the WMA's evidence, is worth more than the whole RFT round is likely to be

alternatives.option: Sweep temperature 0.2 / 0.4 / 0.7 as well
alternatives.reason: single-sample greedy is the standard best decode for grade-school math and each extra arm is another locked card; if greedy loses, the sweep becomes worth its cost

alternatives.option: Set the decode by passing arguments to evaluate.py
alternatives.reason: evaluate.py must not be modified and exposes no temperature flag; vLLM runs with --generation-config auto, so the checkpoint's own generation_config.json is the only place the decode can be set - which also means the final_model directory carries it into the graded run

alternatives.option: Retrain with a lower-entropy objective instead
alternatives.reason: a training change cannot be attributed if the decode is still sampling; fix the measurement instrument first

alternatives.option: Rejection-sampling round (sample k solutions from exp-02 on 44k train questions, keep the correct ones)
alternatives.reason: measured at 6,000 output tok/s the 43k-generation sweep needs ~73 min of GPU before a single gradient step, and it distils the 4B model into itself; the discarded OpenMathInstruct-2 solutions are the same 'many correct chains per problem' signal from a 405B teacher, and cost 2 min of CPU instead. Kept as the fallback if this card fails.

alternatives.option: Retrain from base on 200k rows instead of continuing from exp-02/final
alternatives.reason: ~3 h against ~1 h, and it throws away a checkpoint already measured at 0.6533

alternatives.option: Two more epochs over the same sft_v1.jsonl
alternatives.reason: repeating identical (question, solution) pairs is the memorisation path; every row here is a pair exp-02 never saw

alternatives.option: Raise the learning rate back to 1e-5
alternatives.reason: the parent has already converged to loss 0.605; a second pass at the original LR risks washing out the format behaviour that took the score from 0.073 to 0.593. 5e-6 with a short warmup is the conservative continuation.

alternatives.option: Skip the sweep and launch exp-04's continuation straight away
alternatives.reason: exp-04 is already locked and will be launched either way, but these two checkpoints are on disk, cost ~5 min of GPU each, and are the only untried route to a better incumbent that requires no training at all

alternatives.option: Score them under the inherited sampling decode to save the variant step
alternatives.reason: exp-03 adopted greedy; a comparator measured under a different decode is not a comparator

alternatives.option: Also sweep exp-04's checkpoints in this card
alternatives.reason: exp-04 has not run yet - its checkpoints do not exist, and a card cannot name evidence it does not have

alternatives.option: Resolve the tie at --limit -1 now and skip merging
alternatives.reason: that read is planned as the next card either way; running it first would spend ~40 min without adding a candidate, and if the soup wins it would have to be re-run anyway

alternatives.option: A third round of SFT on new data
alternatives.reason: exp-04 bought +4.0 points against exp-03 for an hour of H100 and still only tied a free checkpoint; with 5.3 h left, an unproven fourth data source is a worse bet than a 5-minute average of models already measured

alternatives.option: Rejection-sampling round
alternatives.reason: still the standing fallback, but it needs ~73 min of sampling plus ~40 min of training before it can be read, and the endgame needs ~1.5 h reserved for full-n selection and final_model assembly

alternatives.option: Weighted average favouring the two 0.6933 members
alternatives.reason: the weights would be fitted on the same n=150 reads that cannot separate the members; a uniform average has no free parameter to overfit

alternatives.option: Average in the base model or exp-04's checkpoint-600
alternatives.reason: the base model is not a fine-tune of the same task and would drag the soup off the format behaviour; checkpoint-600 is a strictly earlier point on exp-04's own path and scored 0.6667

alternatives.option: Ship whichever of the two is cheaper to assemble and skip the read
alternatives.reason: the two arms were produced by different data and an hour of training separates them; shipping a coin flip when the ruler that resolves it costs 40 minutes and 5.0 h remain is the one avoidable way to lose points here

alternatives.option: Break the tie on dev300
alternatives.reason: exp-04 trained on MetaMathQA rephrasings of GSM8K train problems, which exact-string exclusion does not remove from dev300, so that probe leaks to one arm only - flagged in exp-04's verdict and again in exp-06's card

alternatives.option: Repeat the n=150 read on each arm (C18)
alternatives.reason: greedy decoding is deterministic; the same weights return the same 104. Only more items move this floor - the manual puts the greedy n=150 repeat spread at 1.3 points

alternatives.option: Also read the soup and exp-02/final at --limit -1
alternatives.reason: the soup was rejected at 3.3 points below both candidates with degraded stopping behaviour, and exp-02/final is 4 points below at n=150; spending 40 more minutes to rank models already behind would eat the assembly-and-verification budget

alternatives.option: Start a rejection-sampling round with the remaining hours instead
alternatives.reason: ~2 h from launch to a readable number, and it would then need its own full-limit read to be adoptable; that does not fit in front of final_model assembly, which must not be rushed (pitfall final_model_not_loadable)

alternatives.option: Re-run the rejection-sampling round with the suspected bug fixed
alternatives.reason: the 23.4% pass@4 is far below what a 0.69-accuracy model should produce, and the likely cause is that vLLM's LLM.generate() tokenises raw text with add_special_tokens=True on top of a template that already emits <bos>, giving a doubled BOS. The 15 min probe meant to confirm that hit the tool timeout and returned nothing. Re-sampling is ~30 min against an unconfirmed diagnosis with 3.2 h left, and the 1,974 rows that did verify against gold are correct regardless of how they were sampled, so they are kept and the rest of the round is dropped.

alternatives.option: Stop now and ship the banked model
alternatives.reason: the honest default, and it stays the outcome unless this card wins outright. But 28,715 clean rows and a 25-minute training run fit inside the buffer with over an hour to spare, and rejecting costs only time

alternatives.option: Another weight average
alternatives.reason: exp-06 already tested that on this tree and it came in 3.3 points below its members with degraded stopping behaviour

alternatives.option: Include the 5,496 questions the sampler failed to solve as hard negatives
alternatives.reason: there is no verified correct solution for them - that list is a record of what the sampler could not do, not training data

alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and start SFT immediately
alternatives.reason: every later card needs a comparator measured under the same protocol (pitfall comparator_protocol_mismatch); ~20 min now buys that for the whole batch

alternatives.option: Baseline at --limit 500 for a tighter CI
alternatives.reason: 10-shot prompts are ~1.4k tokens; 500 items costs a large slice of the 10h budget. n=150 is the harness default and will be the dev protocol for every card in this batch

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full-parameter SFT
alternatives.reason: the model must learn a turn/stop behaviour it has never seen; full FT fits in 80 GB here (measured in the smoke run) and LoRA adds a merge step that is a known way to ship an unloadable final_model

alternatives.option: Train on GSM8K train reference solutions only (7.4k rows)
alternatives.reason: 7.4k terse reference chains fix the format but leave reasoning at the base model's level; OpenMathInstruct-2's GSM8K-derived solutions are longer self-checking chains from a much stronger generator. Both are used, mixed.

alternatives.option: MetaMathQA as the augmentation source
alternatives.reason: its bodies carry GSM8K's own '#### N' line plus 'The answer is: N', i.e. two extra answer markers to strip (pitfall double_answer_format), and its generator is weaker than OpenMathInstruct-2's. Kept in scripts/build_data.py as a fallback source, weight 0 here.

alternatives.option: Put the grader's exact 10-shot system message on every training row
alternatives.reason: it is ~1.6k tokens against a ~180-token answer, so >85% of the compute would go to a frozen prefix. Instead 10% of rows carry that exact prefix, 20% carry a random 2-5 shot prefix, 70% are zero-shot.

alternatives.option: Retrain from base on the larger sft_v2 corpus (77k rows, already built and decontaminated)
alternatives.reason: 2 epochs from base is 3.2 h of the 7 h left and only scales the same off-policy distribution; the measured residual is reasoning error on items the model gets wrong, which off-policy data addresses only indirectly. sft_v2 stays on disk as the fallback if this card fails.

alternatives.option: DPO/GRPO on correct-vs-incorrect samples
alternatives.reason: no preference/RL trainer is set up and a first RL run inside 7 h with one GPU is a poor bet against a method that reliably gives single-digit gains; RFT is the same signal (verifier = the known answer) at SFT cost

alternatives.option: Keep only self-generated correct samples
alternatives.reason: 2770 questions are solved by none of the 4 draws - exactly the hard tail. Their dataset reference solutions are added as hard_ref rows so the run also sees what it currently cannot produce.

alternatives.option: Train on RFT rows alone with no replay
alternatives.reason: continuing on self-generated text only risks narrowing the distribution; 10k rows of the exp-02 corpus are mixed back in as replay

alternatives.option: Another training round (fresh off-policy data, or a second RFT round)
alternatives.reason: the cheapest useful training run left is ~1 h plus evaluation, and 4.2 h has to also cover the n=500 confirmation and packaging final_model. A soup is ~15 min, so it is run first and a training round is only attempted with what is left.

alternatives.option: Weighted soup sweep (0.25/0.5/0.75)
alternatives.reason: each extra weight costs a full re-merge plus a 5 min eval and would be a separate card; one uniform average is the single highest-prior point and this card tests exactly that

alternatives.option: Soup exp-02/ep1 with exp-02/final
alternatives.reason: exp-02/ep1 is a strictly worse mid-cosine point on the same run (0.660) with no evidence of complementary strengths; exp-03/final is a genuinely different training signal (its own verified samples)

alternatives.option: A second RFT round from the soup
alternatives.reason: exp-03 measured that intervention on this model and it lost 4.7 pts; repeating it with 3.9 h left is not a good bet

alternatives.option: Two epochs over the fresh mix
alternatives.reason: 2 epochs is ~1.7 h and would leave no room for the n=500 confirmation and packaging. exp-03 also showed epoch 2 of a continuation is where the loss curve drops and the score does not.

alternatives.option: Restart from base on all 77k rows
alternatives.reason: 3.2 h for 2 epochs, more than the whole remaining budget once evaluation and packaging are counted

alternatives.option: Continue from exp-02/final rather than from the soup
alternatives.reason: the soup is the point-estimate incumbent at 0.720 and continuing from the best available start is what a further gain would have to build on; the exp-02 lineage stays on disk either way

alternatives.option: Any further training run
alternatives.reason: 2.7 h left has to cover the n=500 selection (~40 min) and packaging; the shortest useful training round measured in this batch was 0.9 h and the last two both came back flat or negative

alternatives.option: Uniform average of the three distinct training endpoints (exp-02/final, exp-03/final, exp-05/final)
alternatives.reason: that puts weight 1/3 on exp-03/final, the weakest checkpoint measured (0.660). Averaging the two best candidates gives exp-03 weight 0.25 through the exp-04 soup, which is the weight that has already been shown to work.

alternatives.option: A weight sweep over the two ingredients
alternatives.reason: each point is a re-merge plus a 5 min eval and would be its own card; at 2.7 h the uniform point is the only one that fits before the selection run

alternatives.option: Submit exp-06/soup on the n=150 read alone
alternatives.reason: the adoption rule fixed before exp-04's eval says a gap at or inside ~3 pt is not distinguishable at n=150 and must not by itself decide the submission; 3.3 pt is exactly at that boundary

alternatives.option: Score at --limit -1 (all 1319 test items)
alternatives.reason: ~35 min per arm against 2.5 h left, and it would leave no margin for packaging and the final CPU load check. n=500 cuts the stderr from ~3.7 to ~2.0 pt, which is enough to resolve a 3 pt gap.

alternatives.option: Also score exp-05/final and exp-02/final at n=500
alternatives.reason: both are strictly below the two arms here on dev-150 and neither can become the submission unless one of these two also loses; ~12 min each is not worth it with 2.5 h left

alternatives.option: One more soup or training round instead
alternatives.reason: nothing further would be validated before the deadline; an unvalidated artifact is not a better submission than a validated one

alternatives.option: Trust the cp -r and ship without serving final_model/
alternatives.reason: the whole batch's value rides on one directory loading in a fresh vLLM process; 6 minutes to prove it is the cheapest insurance available

alternatives.option: Verify with a CPU transformers load only
alternatives.reason: that was already done for the earlier artifact and it does not exercise vLLM's config/tokenizer path, model_type() detection in evaluate.py, or the generation_config that makes decoding greedy

alternatives.option: Verify at n=500 instead of n=150
alternatives.reason: this card asks whether the directory serves and reproduces, not what the model scores; n=150 has an exact expected value to compare against (0.7533, same weights, same invocation) and costs a third as much

alternatives.option: Evaluate exp-05/final and exp-02/final at n=500 with the remaining time instead
alternatives.reason: both are below the two arms already scored, and adding candidates to a max-of-noisy-estimates selection increases winner's-curse bias rather than the expected score

alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and compare later SFT runs only against each other
alternatives.reason: Without a parent number I cannot tell whether SFT helped or hurt, and rule 2 of the protocol requires a comparator measured under the same protocol.

alternatives.option: Run the baseline at --limit 500 for tighter error bars
alternatives.reason: 10-shot prompts are ~1700 tokens; 500 items costs ~3x the wall time and the whole batch is 10 h. n=150 is the harness default and is what every later card will use.

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of full fine-tuning
alternatives.reason: the failure is a behaviour the base model was never trained for at all (answer the last turn, stop at <end_of_turn>); full FT fits in 80 GB once the loss is taken over labelled positions only, and there is no adapter-merge step to get wrong before the deadline.

alternatives.option: Decode-config only (ship temperature 0.0 and keep base weights)
alternatives.reason: cannot fix a model that answers a question it invented; folded into this card for free instead, since the trained checkpoint writes its own generation_config.

alternatives.option: Train on gsm8k train alone (7473 rows)
alternatives.reason: too few rows and only terse human CoT; OpenMathInstruct-2's gsm8k/augmented_gsm8k split adds 148k verified verbose solutions over GSM8K-train-derived problems at no contamination cost.

alternatives.option: MetaMathQA
alternatives.reason: its bodies carry gsm8k's own '#### N' line as well as a boxed answer - the double_answer_format pitfall - and would need the same rewriting as OMI-2 with worse provenance.

alternatives.option: Rejection-sampling FT on exp-02's own correct chains (RFT), now
alternatives.reason: also promising, but it should be run on top of the best supervised model rather than under it: an RFT round taken from a stronger parent samples better chains. Scheduled as the next card once this one reports (sampling ~0.7 h + training ~1 h fits the remaining budget after this run).

alternatives.option: Raise the learning rate or the epoch count on sft_v1
alternatives.reason: exp-02's loss curve is smooth with grad_norm 1.2-4.1 and epoch 2 still gained +4.0 pts, so the run is not obviously mis-tuned; changing data volume is the larger lever and keeps this card to one variable.

alternatives.option: Add OpenMathInstruct-2's math / augmented_math splits
alternatives.reason: MATH-style problems bring LaTeX-heavy targets and non-numeric answers that the numeric grader cannot read; they would change the target distribution rather than deepen the GSM8K one.

alternatives.option: microsoft/orca-math-word-problems-200k for problem diversity
alternatives.reason: no verified answer field - the gold answer would have to be scraped from free text, so a fraction of rows would carry wrong labels. OMI-2's rows are already answer-verified.

alternatives.option: Keep the n=150 ruler and 1.5 epochs, as this card was first written
alternatives.reason: the WMA verdict's tier-4 precondition is right: n=150 has a 3.8 pt stderr while this card's own predicted effect is +2 to +6 pts, so the likeliest outcome was a number nobody could read. Re-scoring the incumbent on the full 1319-item test set costs 2.6 min and gives a 1.3 pt ruler. Both the protocol and the comparator were changed and the card re-locked before launch.

alternatives.option: 1.5 epochs on sft_v2 (the original plan)
alternatives.reason: it would be 1.82x exp-02's optimizer steps, so data volume and compute would move together and a positive result would not be attributable. 1.0 epoch on sft_v2 is 134946 samples against exp-02's 110946, i.e. 1.22x the tokens for 2.4x the distinct problems - close to the pure data-volume change this card claims to be. It also matches the corpus pattern the verdict cites, that scaled-up mixtures win at 1 epoch and lose at 2, and it returns 0.8 h to the RFT card.

alternatives.option: A second epoch of sft_v2 from base (2 x 900 steps)
alternatives.reason: 2.9 h of the 5.0 h left for a lever the corpus reports as negative on scaled-up mixtures, and it would not touch the boundary-item problem this card is aimed at. The RFT round costs 0.7 h of training on data already generated.

alternatives.option: DPO / preference pairs from the correct-vs-incorrect samples
alternatives.reason: the samples are there and pairs would be cheap to form, but a DPO run is a new trainer, a new loss and a new set of failure modes with 5 h left and no smoke; RFT reuses the exact SFT path that has now produced two working checkpoints.

alternatives.option: RFT rows only, with no replay of the supervised mixture
alternatives.reason: on-policy-only continuation narrows the output distribution and risks losing the few-shot-prefixed rows entirely (RFT prompts are all 0-shot, while the graded prompt carries 10 shots). 24000 sft_v2 rows are mixed back in, which keeps ~12% few-shot rows in the stream.

alternatives.option: The first mix (scripts/mix_data.py, unstratified 24000-row replay)
alternatives.reason: the WMA verdict's tier-1 precondition caught it: because every RFT row is generated 0-shot, that mix carried only 4.9% k-shot rows (462 at 10 shots) while the grader always prompts with 10 shots, so the card's own rationale for the replay slice was not met. Rebuilt with scripts/remix_v3.py to 12.77% (1223 at 10 shots) and re-locked before launch.

alternatives.option: Keep every correct sample rather than capping per question
alternatives.reason: it would weight the corpus toward the easy questions the model already solves 6/6 times. --adaptive-keep instead keeps 1 chain when the pass rate is >=0.75, 2 in the middle band and 3 when it is <=0.25, spending the budget on the boundary.

alternatives.option: A second RFT round with a stronger accept gate (majority-vote agreement across the k samples)
alternatives.reason: this is the right fix for why exp-04's mechanism failed, but it needs a fresh sampling pass (0.65 h) plus training (0.6 h) plus eval, which is the whole remaining budget with nothing left for final verification of final_model/.

alternatives.option: Score exp-03's checkpoint-300 / checkpoint-600 (the C5 checkpoint-selection lever)
alternatives.reason: both sit mid-cosine at a high learning rate, and the one mid-cosine checkpoint already measured (exp-02's epoch-1 at 0.6333 vs its final 0.6733) was clearly worse. Low prior, and each read costs 3 min.

alternatives.option: Do nothing further and spend the remaining time on verification
alternatives.reason: verification needs ~0.3 h, not 3 h. The soup leaves well over an hour of slack and cannot damage the incumbent: promote.py refuses anything that does not beat 0.6770 at n=1319.

alternatives.option: A second RFT round with a majority-vote accept gate
alternatives.reason: it is the right diagnosis of why exp-04 failed, but a fresh sampling pass is 0.65 h on top of 0.6 h of training and there are 2.8 h left including final verification of final_model/. This card reuses the RFT chains already generated instead.

alternatives.option: A second full epoch of sft_v2 from exp-03
alternatives.reason: 1.45 h, and exp-04 was already a continuation of exp-03 that included 24000 sft_v2 rows and gained nothing measurable. Changing what the data is about has more headroom left than seeing the same data again.

alternatives.option: Training from the base snapshot rather than continuing from exp-04
alternatives.reason: 1 epoch from base on 58k rows was never as good as the 135k run (exp-02's 55k-row 2-epoch run reached 0.6505 against exp-03's 0.6725); continuing keeps everything exp-03 and exp-04 learned and spends the whole budget on the new distribution. The cost is that a gain will be attributable to 'this mixture applied last', not to the mixture in isolation.

alternatives.option: Downloading more OpenMathInstruct-2 shards for a 200k-row run
alternatives.reason: 1 epoch on 200k rows is 2.2 h, which would leave no time to verify the submission.

alternatives.option: Add more real-distribution problems instead of re-reading these
alternatives.reason: there are only 7473 real GSM8K train problems and all of them are already in the mixture. Anything else (orca-math, more OMI-2 shards) is another synthetic distribution, which is the thing exp-06 showed is worth less - and a new source would need building, contamination-checking and a full epoch inside 1.9 h.

alternatives.option: Score exp-06's checkpoint-200 (the C5 checkpoint-selection lever)
alternatives.reason: cheap, but it sits mid-cosine at a high LR and the one mid-cosine checkpoint measured in this batch (exp-02's epoch-1 at 0.6333 against its final 0.6733) was clearly worse. Low prior for a card's worth of overhead.

alternatives.option: The original plan: a second annealed pass over sft_v4_gold from exp-06/final at lr 3e-6
alternatives.reason: killed by its own precondition. exp-06/checkpoint-200 scores 0.7040 and its endpoint 0.7013, so the mixture is already saturated and a further anneal off the endpoint has nothing to fit. Re-locked rather than launched.

alternatives.option: Promote exp-06/checkpoint-200 (0.7040) over exp-06/final (0.7013)
alternatives.reason: a 0.27 pt gap on a ruler that resolves 1.3 pts is a tie. This card's own promotion rule - fixed before launch - says a gap inside the ruler does not justify a swap, and applying it to a number that flatters me would make it worthless when it does not.

alternatives.option: Re-annealing from checkpoint-200 rather than from the endpoint
alternatives.reason: the verdict's other branch, and defensible, but it stacks a parent change on top of the data change and tests the saturated mixture again. Keeping the parent identical to exp-06's makes this a clean single-variable read of the replay share.

alternatives.option: MetaMathQA as the new-problem source

alternatives.option: More rows (160-200k) for a stronger single model
alternatives.reason: 200k rows is ~2.6 h and would leave no room for the merge, the reads or packaging; 120k is the largest size that fits with slack

alternatives.option: Quote the published Gemma-3-4B-PT GSM8K number (38.4, 5-shot) as comparator
alternatives.reason: different protocol (5-shot, different harness); a number from a different protocol is not a comparator

alternatives.option: Skip the baseline and compare the SFT run against nothing
alternatives.reason: no way to tell an improvement from a regression, and no way to detect a broken eval harness before spending GPU hours on training

alternatives.option: Go straight to SFT to save ~20 min of GPU time
alternatives.reason: the eval harness is unverified; a first run that silently mis-renders the chat template would cost far more than 20 min

alternatives.option: LoRA instead of a full fine-tune
alternatives.reason: the model has to learn a new output contract (stop after the answer) as well as arithmetic; full FT fits in 80 GB once the loss is computed only at supervised positions, and LoRA is the fallback if it does not

alternatives.option: Train only on the 7473 human GSM8K train solutions
alternatives.reason: too few and too terse to move a 4B much; they are included, but 112k Llama-3.1-405B solutions to GSM8K-train problems and to LLM-generated augmentations of them give far more coverage of the same problem distribution

alternatives.option: Train purely zero-shot on the eval's user template
alternatives.reason: the harness always runs fewshot=10, so 12% of rows carry a 1-10 exemplar system prefix drawn from the GSM8K TRAIN split to keep the eval-time prompt shape in distribution

alternatives.option: One epoch now, decide about the second later
alternatives.reason: a single cosine schedule over both epochs is better-conditioned than two restarts, and saving at the epoch-1 boundary gives the same choice without paying for a second warmup

alternatives.option: MetaMathQA as the corpus
alternatives.reason: its bodies carry GSM8K's own four-hash answer line as well as a boxed answer, which is the documented double_answer_format pitfall; OpenMathInstruct-2 needs only a boxed-to-plain rewrite

alternatives.option: Leave the decode alone and spend the 15 minutes on more training data
alternatives.reason: the two are not exclusive and this one is nearly free: no weights change, one eval, and it also fixes the run-to-run noise that every later comparison has to see through

alternatives.option: Tune a middle temperature (0.2-0.4) or a min_p floor
alternatives.reason: that is a sweep, not an experiment, and each arm costs another eval; greedy is the single decode that maximises pass@1 for a fixed model and is the one worth one card

alternatives.option: Change the eval command instead of the checkpoint
alternatives.reason: forbidden - evaluate.py and templates/ are immutable. The decode has to travel with the model artifact, which is where a released model's recommended decode belongs anyway

alternatives.option: A third epoch on the same data/sft_120k.jsonl
alternatives.reason: the model has already seen every one of those 120k targets twice; new solutions to the same problems carry information a repeat does not, and cost the same

alternatives.option: Rejection-sampling fine-tuning on the model's own correct samples
alternatives.reason: costs ~40 min of generation before any training starts and the resulting targets are weaker than what is already available: 411k unused Llama-3.1-405B solutions, answer-verified, sit on disk. RFT is the next card if this one stalls

alternatives.option: More unique problems rather than more solutions per problem
alternatives.reason: measured and unavailable. Parsing the whole 14M-row OpenMathInstruct-2 train split found 2.57M GSM8K-derived rows but only 117 problems the exp-02 pool did not already have (logs/build_full.log), so the entire corpus covers ~80.8k unique problems. More solutions per problem is the only axis that exists

alternatives.option: Add the augmented_math subset for algebra coverage
alternatives.reason: one of the observed failures is an algebra setup, but MATH-style targets are long and LaTeX-heavy and would shift the output distribution away from the short GSM8K chains that are now scoring; not worth the risk on the last training run with time for one

alternatives.option: 200k new rows instead of 130k
alternatives.reason: 2.6 h of training against 1.7 h, and with 5.65 h left that leaves no room to evaluate, package and verify - the marginal solutions are the least valuable part of the pool anyway

alternatives.option: Stop here and spend the remaining time on a larger-n confirmation of exp-04
alternatives.reason: with 3.6 h left there is room for one more 1.4 h training run and still an hour of slack; a wider read narrows the error bar on a number but does not improve the model, and exp-04 already cleared its threshold by twice the noise floor

alternatives.option: Weight-average exp-02/final with exp-04/final (model soup)
alternatives.reason: soup.py is written and costs ~10 min, but averaging a checkpoint with its own worse ancestor (0.7533 vs 0.8267 greedy) is far more likely to interpolate backwards than forwards; kept as the fallback if this run has to be abandoned

alternatives.option: 200k rows for a larger step
alternatives.reason: 2.6 h against 3.6 h remaining leaves no room to evaluate, export and verify final_model; 110k is sized so that the run, its eval and the packaging all fit with an hour to spare

alternatives.option: Rejection-sampling fine-tuning on the incumbent's own samples
alternatives.reason: still the right next line if the SFT corpus flattens, but it needs ~40 min of generation before the first training step and the corpus has not flattened yet

alternatives.option: Declare the session finished on the 0.8267 read
alternatives.reason: the one link never tested is the exact invocation the deliverable is graded under; a final_model that only works at the flags I happened to choose is the final_model_not_loadable pitfall wearing a different hat

alternatives.option: A larger-n read (--limit 400) to narrow the error bar instead
alternatives.reason: ~25 min for a better-measured number that changes no decision - there is nothing left to choose between. Confirming the artifact loads and scores at the default invocation is the only remaining question whose answer could still cost the whole run

alternatives.option: Weight-average exp-04 with exp-05 (model soup)
alternatives.reason: the only untried lever left, but the adoption rule needs a delta above +0.031 and the harness has just been shown to move +-0.02 on identical weights; a single n=150 read cannot license that decision in the time left, and a rushed overwrite of a verified final_model is the worse risk
